title: Virtual reception services for lead qualification: compare
description: Compare receptionist services by qualification rules, rejected and uncertain inquiries, delivered records and the evidence your office needs to act.
lead: Buy a decision trail and usable handoff, not a qualified-lead label.
intro: This comparison examines Smith.ai, AnswerConnect and Ruby by how documented screening becomes an office handoff. It covers rule design, delivery and uncertain answers, rather than repeating an intake question list. Published by Revo; official sources checked October 23, 2026. No qualified-lead yield or conversion improvement was measured.

sections.title: Smith.ai: explicit screening decisions and a separate intake stage
paragraphs: Smith.ai’s current screening page describes custom criteria, AI-first intake and human escalation for complex situations, with dashboard notes, summaries and call metadata. Its dated March 26, 2025 product announcement describes up to three yes/no qualification questions in addition to location/service screening, with a disqualifying answer ending the call. Confirm current package limits; the older announcement is evidence of that documented design, not a universal limit on all intake today.

This is a useful candidate when the business wants explicit decision gates. Ask it to show the actual rule order and the record for a rejected caller, not only a successful intake. A vague answer such as “I think the property is in your area” must have a reviewed handling rule; do not silently convert uncertainty into a negative answer. Confirm the human handoff scope and terms for your chosen AI or staffed package.
items: Request: applied rule version, answer captured, screening decision and exception reason.
Keep qualification gates separate from the longer intake questions asked after a caller passes.

sections.title: AnswerConnect: live scripted scoring against your criteria
paragraphs: AnswerConnect’s inbound-sales service describes a team using a scripting tool to score leads against client criteria and customize scripts during setup. Its small-business explanation says receptionists screen using your criteria and send the details afterward. Those descriptions establish a staffed screening model, not a particular home-service scoring formula or a guaranteed qualified lead.

Shortlist it if a person working from your scoring policy is important. Supply the score inputs, mandatory disqualifiers and the treatment of missing answers. Ask for the exact delivered fields and destination, including the record for an inquiry that fails the score. The reviewed pages do not specify a portable rule-version audit field or your CRM mapping; treat those as demonstration requirements.
items: Separate mandatory service-area exclusion from a preference such as requested timing.
Require an unscored or needs-review path when a required answer is unavailable.

sections.title: Ruby: configurable information collection with live reception
paragraphs: Ruby documents live receptionists, call handling instructions that can be updated, lead capture and notifications through email, text or its app. Its plan page says the information collected can be customized. These sources do not establish a specific numerical scoring engine or the same automatic rejection behavior as the Smith.ai announcement.

Shortlist Ruby when live collection and an accountable office decision are more important than a published scoring mechanism. Ask what the receptionist may decide and what remains a message for your team. Demonstrate a caller who changes an answer, an existing customer misidentified as a new prospect and a request needing a specialist; confirm the resulting notification contains the uncertainty rather than an unsupported qualified label.
items: Confirm the actual questions and call handling update process.
Request a sample delivered message and prove that the responsible person can retrieve it.

sections.title: Compare the same evidence packet from every finalist
paragraphs: Use this original fictional acceptance case: the business serves residential properties in its approved ZIP list and offers plumbing repairs but not restoration work. The caller reports water damage, cannot yet confirm the service address and asks for a repair visit. The correct business decision is not supplied by a vendor’s qualified label: preserve the missing address, the requested work and the boundary between plumbing and restoration for office review.

Ask each finalist for one example that passes all mandatory rules, one clearly outside the service area and the uncertain example above. Compare the original answers, applied rule version, decision with reason, unresolved field, delivery destination and named follow-up owner. A CRM contact created without those details is a different deliverable from a reviewable screening record.

Repeat the uncertain case after a documented rule change and check that the new version governs it. This is a proposed evaluation protocol, not a claim that any listed provider already exports every field. Confirm what is included, requires configuration or is unavailable before selecting a plan.
items: Do not count existing-customer service calls as new qualified prospects.
Ask how rejected and uncertain inquiries remain available for review.
A screening decision does not promise a booking, completed job or revenue.

Dashboard notes, summaries and call metadata

faqs.q: Does qualified mean the caller will buy?
faqs.a: No. It describes a screening decision under the chosen rules. Availability, follow-up and the customer’s decision remain separate.

faqs.q: How should missing answers affect a score?
faqs.a: Define that with your business before setup. Preserve an unknown value and a needs-review path rather than assuming missing means no.

faqs.q: Are all compared services automatic lead-scoring products?
faqs.a: No. The comparison distinguishes explicit gates, live scripted scoring and configurable live collection. Verify the exact mechanism and output in the proposed package.

takeaway: Select the service that delivers a reviewable decision and assigns the next action under your rules.

title: AI answering for HVAC and plumbing: feature comparison
description: Compare AI answering for HVAC and plumbing by job permissions, booking records, existing appointments and the route for urgent or unbooked calls.
lead: Compare what gets booked, what gets changed and what still needs your dispatcher.
intro: Compare ServiceTitan AI Voice Agent, Avoca, Sameday and Rosie against the call operations an HVAC or plumbing office must control. The matrix separates documented functions from account-specific questions. Published by Revo; sources checked October 23, 2026. It is not a test ranking, technical diagnosis guide or guarantee that a technician will be dispatched.

sections.title: ServiceTitan Voice Agent: permission and job-type controls
paragraphs: ServiceTitan’s Basic Phones/Phones Pro setup guide, updated October 22, marks the feature Early Access for specific accounts. Booking, rescheduling and cancellation require both the overall capability and the applicable job-type toggle. This is a concrete control to check when plumbing repairs may be booked but installation estimates follow a different policy.

Its FAQ describes unbooked-call follow-up tags and email summaries. The same FAQ still lists a launch limitation on adding notes, summaries or transcripts to booked job records. Ask the provider to reconcile that limitation for your account rather than assuming a call summary is attached to every booked job. The setup guide directs configuration of Adaptive Capacity; confirm readiness and account eligibility before comparing it as an available option.
items: Demonstrate an enabled repair job type and a disabled install type.
Verify reschedule/cancel permission separately from new booking permission.

sources.label: ServiceTitan FAQ and current documented limitations

sections.title: Avoca: compare the job record and CSR handoff
paragraphs: Avoca’s ServiceTitan page describes sending customer details, appointment times, service information, booking source and conversation notes to ServiceTitan. Its inbound page describes contextual escalation to a CSR. Neither description establishes that every account has the same permissions to change or cancel an existing appointment.

For an HVAC/plumbing evaluation, request the exact record produced for a repair, maintenance visit and estimate. Then ask for an appointment-change case and an integration write failure. Require the proposed scope to identify whether the service changes the record, captures a request or escalates it. A transcript saying “booked” is insufficient if the job did not arrive in the authoritative system.
items: Check the service type, address and appointment on the actual returned job record.
Identify the receiving CSR and the fallback when that person is unavailable.

sections.title: Sameday: distinguish trade workflow from confirmed field availability

title: Plan 24/7 phone coverage: shifts, peaks and backup owners
description: Build a weekly phone-coverage plan with time windows, peak triggers, absence backups and accountable follow-up, using a blank CSV and fictional week.
lead: Account for every interval and test the person or service expected to answer.

sections.title: Measure demand by interval before assigning the week
paragraphs: Collect your own call arrivals and handling time by interval, including simultaneous demand, unanswered calls and work performed after the conversation. Separate new requests from existing-customer work. A monthly total cannot show whether a quiet night and a short morning burst need different handling.

Amazon Connect’s documentation distinguishes forecasting contact volume and handle time, capacity planning and individual scheduling. Its time-zone documentation also distinguishes forecast/download time zones. Those product concepts inform the planning questions here; neither Amazon scheduling nor workforce automation is asserted as a Revo feature.

Use one explicit operating time zone and dates in your worksheet. Choose interval lengths that expose your observed peaks. The example uses four six-hour blocks only to illustrate the assignment ledger; split those blocks where your records show a peak, break, training session or change of owner. sections.title: Fill the coverage ledger and keep verification separate
paragraphs: The blank CSV contains headers only. The fictional example contains 28 rows for October 26–November 1, 2026 in America/Phoenix, using start-inclusive/end-exclusive hours from 0 to 24. It assigns example roles, never real employees or contact information. Four rows cover each calendar day; the hours add to 168 for that seven-day example, which does not claim the same total for every time zone or daylight-saving week.

Each row identifies the primary answerer, a backup, the unavailable-primary rule, an office-defined peak trigger and peak owner, an authorized urgent-escalation role, the routine-review time and owner, and verification evidence/status. The next routine-review time concerns office follow-up; it is not the time that calls begin to be answered. In this fictional policy, office reviews occur Monday–Friday at 08:00, 12:00 and 18:00. routine_review_at is the first such review at or after the end of the entire row interval, not the review following only its first call. Thus weekday 00–06 goes to 08:00 that same day; 06–12 goes to 12:00; 12–18 goes to 18:00; and overnight/weekend work waits until the next applicable review. Adjust that stated policy to your actual team before use.

Check that each day starts at 0, ends at 24 and has no overlap or gap. Then confirm the named roles correspond to contracted or scheduled coverage. Define the trigger from the system you actually use, such as an agreed queue condition or unavailable primary, and identify who activates extra coverage and who returns the normal route. If no backup is confirmed, mark that interval unresolved and do not describe the plan as reliable 24/7 coverage. Change the assignment or the public expectation before relying on it. This example concerns responsibility and switching, not employment-law advice or a prescribed shift pattern.

The revised-example CSV implements those Tuesday splits: 12–13, 13–14, 14–15 and 15–18 replace the original 12–18 row. It has 31 rows, still covering 168 hours without overlaps. Each split row uses the first scheduled office review at or after its own end; the training and peak rows therefore point to Tuesday 18:00 in this example.

description: Compare SAS, Direct Line and PATLive on message acknowledgement, retry evidence and failed escalation. Use a contractor acceptance ledger before buying.

sections.title: Separate five states before comparing providers
paragraphs:
Use these labels in your service agreement and reporting:

1. **Answered:** the caller spoke with the answering service.
2. **Notification sent:** the service attempted to deliver a message.
3. **Receipt acknowledged:** a recipient explicitly responded.
4. **Responsibility accepted:** an authorized person agreed to own the next business action.
5. **Field action recorded:** your operating system records what happened afterward.

A delivery record can support state two. A reply can support state three. Neither, by itself, establishes that a technician has accepted a job or traveled to the property. Define whether an acknowledgement also accepts business responsibility; otherwise record those decisions separately.

sections.title: Provider comparison: what the documentation establishes
paragraphs:
Reviewed October 23, 2026. These are documentation findings, not live tests. “Unresolved” means the cited page does not establish the requirement, not that the provider cannot support it. Confirm the purchased configuration in writing.

| Provider and evidence | Delivery and acknowledgement | Sequence and retry control | Exhausted-sequence behavior | Audit evidence and unresolved requirements |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [SAS Reach](https://support.specialtyansweringservice.net/article/313-adding-a-reach-message-new) | Voice uses keypad acceptance; SMS uses an explicit reply. | Voice follows scheduled order; SMS supports group or serial delivery with queue intervals and finite attempts. | Recording Reach stops after failed reach. SMS has a limited late-claim window. Serial SMS explicitly lacks an unclaimed-message alert. | Request a sample attempt export and retention terms. Verify the selected message type, failure visibility and business-acceptance meaning. |
| [Direct Line](https://www.directlineanswers.com/emergency-dispatch-services/) | Describes saved message details delivered by text or email, with a reply confirming receipt through its two-way messaging process. | Onboarding defines response instructions; exact intervals and attempt limits are unresolved. | The page does not specify a terminal failure state or who receives it. | Message saving is described; a complete timestamped attempt history, retention and acceptance-owner record need confirmation. |
| [PATLive](https://www.patlive.com/solutions/emergency-dispatch/) | Describes service-request entry into supported service platforms or delivery through email, text and apps. | The dispatch description does not specify an acknowledgement-driven retry sequence. | Failed-escalation handling is unresolved in the dispatch description. | Call/message visibility is described, but recipient acceptance and an escalation-attempt audit need separate verification. |

SAS’s documented acknowledgement mechanism provides a concrete item to demonstrate. Its message-type differences matter: do not assume one failure policy applies to every channel. The same support page notes that Recording Reach depends on call recording being active, and that customer callbacks initiated from voice Reach are billed as patch time. Confirm these dependencies in the proposed setup. [SAS Reach documentation](https://support.specialtyansweringservice.net/article/313-adding-a-reach-message-new)

Direct Line’s documented receipt confirmation is a useful starting point. Ask the provider to demonstrate what occurs after the first unanswered notification, including the final unsuccessful attempt. Do not convert a configurable-response claim into an assumed retry timetable. [Direct Line dispatch service](https://www.directlineanswers.com/emergency-dispatch-services/)

PATLive may fit a process where your service-management system owns the next stage. Establish which system is responsible for acknowledgement and escalation after the request arrives. The page’s separate outbound-calling offer describes a three-attempt limit; that is not evidence of the same limit for dispatch escalation. [PATLive dispatch service](https://www.patlive.com/solutions/emergency-dispatch/)

sections.title: Ask for an attempt ledger, not just a call summary
paragraphs:
A call summary tells the office what the customer said. A proposed attempt ledger should show what happened to the request after that conversation. Keep one request identifier across retries and caller updates, while versioning the message when its contents change.

The following records are fictional design examples, not results from any provider. Times and intervals are illustrative, not recommended response targets.

| Request ID / message version | Policy version | Attempt / UTC time | Target role / channel | Acknowledgement | Accepted owner | Failure or terminal status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DEMO-041 / v1 | ROSTER-07 | 1 / 2026-10-23 22:00 | Primary / voice | None | None | No acknowledgement; sequence continues |
| DEMO-041 / v1 | ROSTER-07 | 2 / 2026-10-23 22:03 | Backup / SMS | Receipt at 22:04 | None yet | Receipt acknowledged; ownership unresolved |
| DEMO-041 / v1 | ROSTER-07 | Ownership event / 22:05 | Backup / authorized office record | Already recorded | Backup technician | Business responsibility accepted; field action unverified |
| DEMO-042 / v1 | ROSTER-07 | Final configured attempt / 22:10 | Duty manager / voice | None | None | Sequence exhausted; exception assigned to office duty lead |

The last row describes a proposed office exception policy, not a vendor feature. The duty lead must be a genuinely staffed role with a documented way to receive and review exceptions. Naming an unattended inbox does not close the operational gap.

For each attempt, preserve the actual timestamp, channel result and recipient role. Record an acknowledgement only when supported by evidence. If a provider cannot export the full ledger, decide whether your own authorized system can reconcile its records without losing the request identifier or inventing a successful delivery.

sections.title: Run four acceptance scenarios before relying on the service
paragraphs:
Use synthetic customer details and a provider-authorized test. Agree on the expected behavior first; leave observed outcomes blank until the demonstration occurs.

| Scenario | Demonstration input | Acceptance evidence to request | Observed result |
|---|---|---|---|
| First recipient unavailable; second accepts | Primary does not respond. Backup acknowledges and separately accepts ownership. | Both attempts, acknowledgement time, accepting role and evidence that later contact stops or follows the agreed rule. | ______ |
| Nobody accepts | All configured recipients remain unavailable through the complete sequence and any late-response window. | Finite attempt count, terminal status, exception destination and proof that failure is visible without a misleading success label. | ______ |
| Shift changes during the sequence | Start under one roster, then activate its successor while a request remains open. | Written decision on whether the request keeps its original roster or migrates; policy version and actual targets recorded. | ______ |
| Caller updates an existing urgent request | Caller supplies a changed access detail while the first message is in progress. | Same request identifier, new message version, which version each recipient saw, and how the accepting owner receives the update. | ______ |

For the all-unavailable case, distinguish “attempts exhausted” from “no further response can be accepted.” Ask whether a late acknowledgement can change the status and how duplicate ownership is prevented. If the service cannot show that boundary, keep the case open for clarification rather than marking the demonstration successful.

The shift-change scenario is equally important. A correct roster at the start does not answer whether an in-progress sequence should continue contacting the outgoing team. Choose a policy your office can maintain and require evidence that the configured process follows it.

sections.title: Get the commercial and operational boundaries in writing
paragraphs:
A useful quote identifies the answering service’s responsibility and the point where your business takes over. Ask the provider to specify:

- Which contact attempts, callbacks, transfers or patch minutes are chargeable.
- Which acknowledgement or on-call functions require an add-on.
- Who updates the roster, how changes take effect, and which time zone governs shifts.
- Whether acknowledging receipt accepts responsibility, or whether a second action is required.
- The retry interval, maximum attempts, late-response handling and final failure destination for each selected channel.
- What evidence is retained, who can access it and how long it remains available.
- How an updated or withdrawn request reaches everyone already notified.

For the surrounding cost questions, review [SAS pricing considerations](/ai-answering-service/specialty-answering-service-pricing), [PATLive pricing considerations](/ai-answering-service/patlive-pricing) and the [Direct Line service guide](/ai-answering-service/direct-line-answering-service). Confirm current terms directly with the provider before contracting.

sections.title: Choose by the unresolved state you need to close
paragraphs:
If your main uncertainty is whether someone received a message, prioritize a demonstrated acknowledgement record. If the uncertainty is whether someone owns the next action, require an explicit acceptance event. If your office already has those functions in its service platform, test the boundary between request entry and that platform’s workflow.

Do not select a provider solely because it answers calls around the clock. Select a configuration that can show what happens when the roster is unavailable, a message changes or a shift ends.

**Prepare the office side of the handoff:** use the [contractor after-hours answering guide](/ai-answering-service/contractors-after-hours-answering) to define intake and responsibility, then bring the four demonstration scenarios above to shortlisted providers. This comparison does not establish any Revo acknowledgement or retry capability.

takeaway: Choose by the unresolved state you need to close

title: Google Local Services Ads answering: routing and lead records
description: Choose answering coverage for Google Local Services Ads by checking the phone route, current missed-call rules and who owns each lead after the conversation.
lead: A paid phone lead needs more than an answered greeting. Someone must capture the request, explain the next step and leave your office with a record it can follow. Before choosing an answering service for Google Local Services Ads, map that entire handoff—not just the number of hours advertised.
intro: A paid phone lead needs more than an answered greeting. Someone must capture the request, explain the next step and leave your office with a record it can follow. Before choosing an answering service for Google Local Services Ads, map that entire handoff—not just the number of hours advertised.

sections.title: Start with the actual phone route
paragraphs:
Google displays a forwarding number that sends the call to your business number. Google also warns that forwarding or VoIP on that business number can prevent you from hearing its “Call from Google” announcement. The absence of that announcement therefore does not prove that a call came from another source. [Google: Manage leads and jobs](https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/6224859?hl=en)

Before changing coverage, write down:

- Which business number receives the ad’s calls.
- Whether the office, a menu or an answering service receives the call next.
- What happens when the office is busy, closed or unable to transfer the call.
- Who owns each configuration and can restore the previous route.

Keep advertising configuration and telephone configuration separate in your notes. An answering provider should demonstrate the supported destination and handoff rather than assume it receives every source field from Google.

sections.title: Understand the current missed-call rules
paragraphs:
Google’s current rules allow charges for missed calls exceeding 20 seconds during business hours. A required IVR routing key starts the timer; later keypresses do not restart it. During business hours, voicemail or greetings without a keypress can be chargeable beyond 20 seconds even without a message. Answered calls are assessed from the conversation, not ring duration. [Google: How leads work](https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/7195435?hl=en)

Do not design a frustrating menu to chase a billing threshold. Choose a route that helps an actual customer explain the requested work and reach the appropriate next step. An answering service cannot promise that a particular call will be free or credited.

sections.title: Match advertised availability to real coverage
paragraphs:
Google defines business hours here using Google Business Profile. When an ad schedule differs, its guidance limits unanswered-call charges to times within both the active schedule and business hours. [Google: How leads work](https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/7195435?hl=en)

Prepare a coverage table for normal hours, lunch breaks, evenings and holidays. For each period, identify the answering owner, permitted booking actions and fallback. Ask the authorized advertising administrator to review mismatches; do not change published hours merely to make a coverage chart look consistent.

Coverage does not mean field availability. A receptionist may capture a request at night while an estimate or service visit still needs office confirmation. Give callers the correct commitment.

sections.title: Keep the lead record separate from the job outcome
paragraphs:
Google’s lead inbox lets businesses review leads and phone interactions. Its records and your answering service’s records serve different purposes. [Google: Manage leads and jobs](https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/6224859?hl=en)

Use an office worksheet with these separate fields:

| Field | What the office should establish |
|---|---|
| Source | Verified LSA lead, another source, or unresolved |
| Call result | Answered, missed, message taken, or transferred |
| Service fit | Requested work and service address checked under your rules |
| Next action | Named owner and callback or scheduling task |
| Booking | Requested window versus confirmed appointment |
| Advertising charge | Status shown by Google, not inferred from the receptionist’s label |

Google exposes charge-status labels, including review and credit states. After a lead is charged, repeat contact from the same phone number or email is not charged again while activity continues within 15 days; 15 inactive days can start a new lead. [Google: How leads work](https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/7195435?hl=en)

For reconciliation, ask which identifiers your actual setup exposes. Use only supported records and authorized access; if the match is uncertain, preserve that uncertainty rather than guessing from a similar timestamp.

sections.title: Require a practical demonstration before committing
paragraphs:
The following are proposed checks, not tests performed by Revo or for this article. Use the providers’ approved diagnostic or sandbox arrangements with authorization. Do not manufacture advertising leads or place chargeable ad calls for a demonstration without explicit authorization.

1. **Ordinary request:** Can the recipient capture the service, address and callback details accurately?
2. **Busy office:** Does the documented backup route receive the call, and who owns the request afterward?
3. **Closed office:** Is the caller told whether a visit is confirmed or only requested?
4. **Unsuccessful transfer:** Does an identifiable person receive the remaining follow-up task?
5. **Missing source announcement:** Can the office still reconcile the record without inventing attribution?
6. **Repeat caller:** Can staff connect the conversation to the existing inquiry rather than duplicate the job?

Record the expected outcome before each demonstration. Review the resulting office record, not just how natural the greeting sounds.

sections.title: Questions to settle with the answering provider
paragraphs:
Ask what happens after intake, which hours and call types are included, what requires your staff, and whether any proposed connection has actually been verified. Confirm who maintains forwarding and how exceptions reach a person.

**Does answering every call remove LSA charges?** No. An answered conversation may still be a valid paid lead. Coverage is about handling the opportunity, not making Google’s billing disappear.

# Google Local Services Ads answering: routing, missed calls and lead records

**Description:** Choose answering coverage for Google Local Services Ads by checking the phone route, current missed-call rules and who owns each lead after the conversation.

A paid phone lead needs more than an answered greeting. Someone must capture the request, explain the next step and leave your office with a record it can follow. Before choosing an answering service for Google Local Services Ads, map that entire handoff—not just the number of hours advertised.

This guide separates Google’s documented rules from proposed operating checks. Documentation was reviewed October 23, 2026. It does not establish a native Revo–Google integration or guarantee lower advertising costs.

## Start with the actual phone route

Google displays a forwarding number that sends the call to your business number. Google also warns that forwarding or VoIP on that business number can prevent you from hearing its “Call from Google” announcement. The absence of that announcement therefore does not prove that a call came from another source. [Google: Manage leads and jobs](https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/6224859?hl=en)

Before changing coverage, write down:

- Which business number receives the ad’s calls.
- Whether the office, a menu or an answering service receives the call next.
- What happens when the office is busy, closed or unable to transfer the call.
- Who owns each configuration and can restore the previous route.

Keep advertising configuration and telephone configuration separate in your notes. An answering provider should demonstrate the supported destination and handoff rather than assume it receives every source field from Google.

## Understand the current missed-call rules

Google’s current rules allow charges for missed calls exceeding 20 seconds during business hours. A required IVR routing key starts the timer; later keypresses do not restart it. During business hours, voicemail or greetings without a keypress can be chargeable beyond 20 seconds even without a message. Answered calls are assessed from the conversation, not ring duration. [Google: How leads work](https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/7195435?hl=en)

Do not design a frustrating menu to chase a billing threshold. Choose a route that helps an actual customer explain the requested work and reach the appropriate next step. An answering service cannot promise that a particular call will be free or credited.

## Match advertised availability to real coverage

Google defines business hours here using Google Business Profile. When an ad schedule differs, its guidance limits unanswered-call charges to times within both the active schedule and business hours. [Google: How leads work](https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/7195435?hl=en)

Prepare a coverage table for normal hours, lunch breaks, evenings and holidays. For each period, identify the answering owner, permitted booking actions and fallback. Ask the authorized advertising administrator to review mismatches; do not change published hours merely to make a coverage chart look consistent.

Coverage does not mean field availability. A receptionist may capture a request at night while an estimate or service visit still needs office confirmation. Give callers the correct commitment.

## Keep the lead record separate from the job outcome

Google’s lead inbox lets businesses review leads and phone interactions. Its records and your answering service’s records serve different purposes. [Google: Manage leads and jobs](https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/6224859?hl=en)

Use an office worksheet with these separate fields:

| Field | What the office should establish |
|---|---|
| Source | Verified LSA lead, another source, or unresolved |
| Call result | Answered, missed, message taken, or transferred |
| Service fit | Requested work and service address checked under your rules |
| Next action | Named owner and callback or scheduling task |
| Booking | Requested window versus confirmed appointment |
| Advertising charge | Status shown by Google, not inferred from the receptionist’s label |

Google exposes charge-status labels, including review and credit states. After a lead is charged, repeat contact from the same phone number or email is not charged again while activity continues within 15 days; 15 inactive days can start a new lead. [Google: How leads work](https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/7195435?hl=en)

For reconciliation, ask which identifiers your actual setup exposes. Use only supported records and authorized access; if the match is uncertain, preserve that uncertainty rather than guessing from a similar timestamp.

## Require a practical demonstration before committing

The following are proposed checks, not tests performed by Revo or for this article. Use the providers’ approved diagnostic or sandbox arrangements with authorization. Do not manufacture advertising leads or place chargeable ad calls for a demonstration without explicit authorization.

1. **Ordinary request:** Can the recipient capture the service, address and callback details accurately?
2. **Busy office:** Does the documented backup route receive the call, and who owns the request afterward?
3. **Closed office:** Is the caller told whether a visit is confirmed or only requested?
4. **Unsuccessful transfer:** Does an identifiable person receive the remaining follow-up task?
5. **Missing source announcement:** Can the office still reconcile the record without inventing attribution?
6. **Repeat caller:** Can staff connect the conversation to the existing inquiry rather than duplicate the job?

Record the expected outcome before each demonstration. Review the resulting office record, not just how natural the greeting sounds.

## Questions to settle with the answering provider

Ask what happens after intake, which hours and call types are included, what requires your staff, and whether any proposed connection has actually been verified. Confirm who maintains forwarding and how exceptions reach a person.

**Does answering every call remove LSA charges?** No. An answered conversation may still be a valid paid lead. Coverage is about handling the opportunity, not making Google’s billing disappear.

**Does this guide verify a Revo integration with Google Local Services Ads?** No. Confirm the supported phone route and record handoff directly with Revo and your phone provider.

**Is a recorded lead a booked job?** No. Booking needs its own evidence and an authorized appointment commitment.

For related decisions, review [dynamic number insertion](https://www.revoapp.ai/ai-answering-service/dynamic-number-insertion), [conditional forwarding](https://www.revoapp.ai/ai-answering-service/conditional-call-forwarding), and [appointment booking](https://www.revoapp.ai/ai-answering-service/appointment-booking). Compare Revo’s current [plans](https://www.revoapp.ai/pricing.html) against the call-handling scope you have established.

sections.title: Keep sensitive details out of ordinary call records
paragraphs:

title: AI receptionist knowledge base: updates and fallback
description: Compare how an AI receptionist uses business information, handles conflicting sources and receives updates before relying on it for customer answers.
lead: Your business may have a current service policy, an old website page and a PDF describing last season’s offer. Giving an AI receptionist access to all three does not establish which answer it should use.
intro: Your business may have a current service policy, an old website page and a PDF describing last season’s offer. Giving an AI receptionist access to all three does not establish which answer it should use.

sections.title: Separate information from instructions and actions
paragraphs:
A greeting tells the receptionist how to introduce the business. A reference answer supplies information about a service. A business record may contain approved hours or locations. A booking action attempts to reserve an actual appointment. Those are different responsibilities.

For example, a page saying that the business offers weekday appointments does not prove that next Tuesday is available. A document describing a warranty does not authorize the receptionist to approve a particular claim. Keep those boundaries visible when discussing the setup with a provider.

Start with this proposed source register:

| Information | Approved owner | What needs checking |
|---|---|---|
| Services offered | Operations lead | Current scope and exclusions |
| Areas served | Office manager | Exceptions and review path |
| Business hours | Office manager | Normal and temporary hours |
| Fee explanation | Authorized business owner | Exact wording and limits; no invented repair quote |
| Booking rules | Scheduling owner | Request versus confirmed appointment |
| Unanswered questions | Service manager | Supported fallback and responsible recipient |

This is an editorial worksheet, not a built-in product feature. Do not add customer-specific records to a general reference collection merely because uploading them is technically possible.

sections.title: Ask which sources the product actually uses
paragraphs:
RingCentral’s hosted AIR skills guide distinguishes generated, editable FAQs from knowledge bases containing website links or documents. It also describes selecting knowledge bases for a receptionist after adding sources to the knowledge hub. That is a useful example of why storing material and attaching it to the active agent are separate checks. [RingCentral-hosted AIR skills guide, pages 5–8](https://assets.ringcentral.com/us/guide/managing-ai-receptionist-skills.pdf)

Jobber describes a different starting point: its receptionist uses business data already in the Jobber account and can be fine-tuned with operating details. That does not mean every field in an account is available for every response. Ask for the documented scope and a demonstration of your specific requirement. [Jobber Receptionist](https://www.getjobber.com/features/ai-receptionist/)

For each shortlisted service, record whether it uses manually approved answers, structured account settings, uploaded files, selected web pages or another documented source. Do not assume that adding a homepage imports every linked page, that a PDF is fully understood, or that a website edit is immediately reflected in answers.

sections.title: Resolve contradictions before asking the AI to resolve them
paragraphs:
Suppose a fictional contractor’s approved policy says that estimates need office review, while an older brochure says all estimates are automatically booked. The first task is to identify and correct the conflicting material—not to add a vague instruction to “always be accurate.”

Ask the provider what happens when sources disagree. If it cannot document a precedence rule, do not invent one in your operating instructions. Remove or exclude stale material through the supported process and keep one approved answer for the consequential policy.

Record the decision, source owner and effective date outside the system if the product does not provide those controls. The point is to maintain a usable evidence trail, not to pretend every receptionist includes version history.

sections.title: Establish the update process before launch
paragraphs:
An uploaded file can be correct today and wrong after a service change. A website source also needs an understood refresh process. Ask these questions before treating source maintenance as included:

- Who may edit answers or attach sources?
- Does a website change require a manual refresh or another documented action?
- How can the office tell that processing is complete and the intended source is active?
- Can an outdated source be disabled or replaced without disabling unrelated answers?
- What is the supported recovery route if a change produces the wrong response?
- Who pays for and performs ongoing maintenance?

RingCentral’s skills guide documents controls to edit, disable or remove individual FAQs and to activate or deactivate its knowledge-base skill. These are product-specific examples of controls to inspect, not a claim that all services offer the same options. [RingCentral-hosted AIR skills guide](https://assets.ringcentral.com/us/guide/managing-ai-receptionist-skills.pdf)

Do not describe a file upload as retraining the underlying AI model unless the provider establishes that this is actually what happens. A business owner generally needs to know which information is consulted and whether the resulting answer is correct—not an unsupported technical label.

sections.title: Check changed answers without involving real customers
paragraphs:
Use a provider-approved non-live test interface where available. RingCentral’s hosted setup guide describes testing an AIR response through chat as well as by calling an extension. It also describes a backup extension setting. These are documented options for that product, not verification that a particular account or Revo includes them. [RingCentral-hosted AIR setup guide, pages 4–7](https://assets.ringcentral.com/us/guide/settingup-updating-your-ai-receptionist.pdf)

The following proposed checks use fictional business details. They are not tests performed for this article:

1. **Known answer:** Ask a straightforward question whose approved answer is present.
2. **Different wording:** Ask the same question conversationally without copying the FAQ.
3. **Missing answer:** Ask for information the business has not supplied. Confirm the approved fallback rather than an invented answer.
4. **Conflicting material:** In an authorized isolated test, inspect how the product handles a known conflict; do not deliberately expose live customers to contradictory policies.
5. **Updated policy:** Change an authorized test source through the supported process and check that the current answer is used.
6. **Action boundary:** Ask for a specific appointment or exception that the reference material cannot authorize.

Record the source version or dated copy, expected answer and observed response. A successful test demonstrates that scenario under that configuration; it is not a guarantee that future answers will always be correct.

sections.title: Make uncertainty an acceptable outcome
paragraphs:
Give the office a practical fallback for unanswered or consequential questions. Depending on the supported setup, that may be a request for review or a transfer to an authorized person. Confirm which action actually occurs and how the office knows it owns the next step.

A caller asking whether an unusual repair is covered should not receive an invented warranty decision. Likewise, intake should not turn a symptom into a diagnosis or a request into an arrival promise. A clear statement that the office needs to review the question can be more useful than a confident but unsupported answer.

sections.title: Compare the maintenance obligation, not just setup speed
paragraphs:
A purchasing demonstration should show how the service handles both an initial approved answer and a later change. Ask what your staff must maintain, which controls are included, and what requires provider support. A fast initial import is not the same as a maintainable process.

**Is a knowledge base the same as a phone script?** No. The script shapes the conversation; the knowledge source supplies reference information. Neither alone establishes permission to complete a transaction or booking.

**Does connecting a website guarantee current answers?** No. Confirm the supported refresh process and verify consequential changes.

**Does this guide establish Revo knowledge-base features?** No. Ask Revo which information sources, editing controls and fallback actions it currently supports.

Use the [phone-answering script guide](https://www.revoapp.ai/ai-answering-service/phone-answering-script) for conversation wording and [call-quality monitoring](https://www.revoapp.ai/ai-answering-service/call-quality-monitoring) for reviewing interactions. Compare [Revo’s current plans](https://www.revoapp.ai/pricing.html) only against capabilities confirmed for your setup.

takeaway: Compare the maintenance obligation, not just setup speed

An uploaded file can be correct today and wrong after a service change. A website source also needs an understood refresh process. Ask these questions before treating source maintenance as included:

- Who may edit answers or attach sources?
- Does a website change require a manual refresh or another documented action?
- How can the office tell that processing is complete and the intended source is active?
- Can an outdated source be disabled or replaced without disabling unrelated answers?
- What is the supported recovery route if a change produces the wrong response?
- Who pays for and performs ongoing maintenance?

RingCentral’s skills guide documents controls to edit, disable or remove individual FAQs and to activate or deactivate its knowledge-base skill. These are product-specific examples of controls to inspect, not a claim that all services offer the same options. [RingCentral-hosted AIR skills guide](https://assets.ringcentral.com/us/guide/managing-ai-receptionist-skills.pdf)

Do not describe a file upload as retraining the underlying AI model unless the provider establishes that this is actually what happens. A business owner generally needs to know which information is consulted and whether the resulting answer is correct—not an unsupported technical label.

## Check changed answers without involving real customers

Use a provider-approved non-live test interface where available. RingCentral’s hosted setup guide describes testing an AIR response through chat as well as by calling an extension. It also describes a backup extension setting. These are documented options for that product, not verification that a particular account or Revo includes them. [RingCentral-hosted AIR setup guide, pages 4–7](https://assets.ringcentral.com/us/guide/settingup-updating-your-ai-receptionist.pdf)

The following proposed checks use fictional business details. They are not tests performed for this article:

1. **Known answer:** Ask a straightforward question whose approved answer is present.
2. **Different wording:** Ask the same question conversationally without copying the FAQ.
3. **Missing answer:** Ask for information the business has not supplied. Confirm the approved fallback rather than an invented answer.
4. **Conflicting material:** In an authorized isolated test, inspect how the product handles a known conflict; do not deliberately expose live customers to contradictory policies.
5. **Updated policy:** Change an authorized test source through the supported process and check that the current answer is used.
6. **Action boundary:** Ask for a specific appointment or exception that the reference material cannot authorize.

Record the source version or dated copy, expected answer and observed response. A successful test demonstrates that scenario under that configuration; it is not a guarantee that future answers will always be correct.

## Make uncertainty an acceptable outcome

Give the office a practical fallback for unanswered or consequential questions. Depending on the supported setup, that may be a request for review or a transfer to an authorized person. Confirm which action actually occurs and how the office knows it owns the next step.

A caller asking whether an unusual repair is covered should not receive an invented warranty decision. Likewise, intake should not turn a symptom into a diagnosis or a request into an arrival promise. A clear statement that the office needs to review the question can be more useful than a confident but unsupported answer.

## Compare the maintenance obligation, not just setup speed

A purchasing demonstration should show how the service handles both an initial approved answer and a later change. Ask what your staff must maintain, which controls are included, and what requires provider support. A fast initial import is not the same as a maintainable process.

**Is a knowledge base the same as a phone script?** No. The script shapes the conversation; the knowledge source supplies reference information. Neither alone establishes permission to complete a transaction or booking.

**Does connecting a website guarantee current answers?** No. Confirm the supported refresh process and verify consequential changes.

**Does this guide establish Revo knowledge-base features?** No. Ask Revo which information sources, editing controls and fallback actions it currently supports.

Use the [phone-answering script guide](https://www.revoapp.ai/ai-answering-service/phone-answering-script) for conversation wording and [call-quality monitoring](https://www.revoapp.ai/ai-answering-service/call-quality-monitoring) for reviewing interactions. Compare [Revo’s current plans](https://www.revoapp.ai/pricing.html) only against capabilities confirmed for your setup.

| Workflow | Input → output | Home-service example | Important boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Capture and conversation | A caller's statements and approved instructions → a structured request or response | Collect a plumbing inquiry for office review | Capture what the caller said; do not turn a symptom into a diagnosis or an unconfirmed visit into a booking. |
| Draft generation | Approved facts and an editing request → proposed text | Rewrite an existing cleaning-service description | A draft is not approved for publication, pricing changes or campaign delivery. |

sections.title: Find a problem before choosing an AI feature
paragraphs:
Write the problem as an observable task: “The office calls people back because requests lack a return number,” rather than “We need AI.” Keep a small, authorized sample of the work that demonstrates the issue. If you cannot show the recurring problem, investigate before buying a tool.

Next, consider a non-AI fix. An intake form, a maintained service-description template or a saved report may solve the same problem. Compare AI against that practical alternative, not against doing nothing.

Use these questions to narrow the choice:

1. **Is the source usable?** Identify the current service list, approved wording or dataset. Conflicting instructions are a cleanup task first, not permission for the tool to choose whichever version it finds.
2. **Can someone check the result?** Name the person who understands the work and can inspect an output against its source. If nobody can judge correctness, defer the workflow.
3. **Does the output stay inside the office?** A draft can wait for review. A spoken promise, sent message or changed customer record may already affect someone before a reviewer sees it.
4. **Can the work return to a manual process?** Describe how to stop the workflow and resolve anything left pending. Deleting an AI draft is different from undoing an appointment change.

Data preparation matters even in purpose-built software. Housecall Pro's CSR AI documentation ties booking behavior to enabled services, service descriptions, booking settings and available windows; it also acknowledges that correct setup does not eliminate every mistake. [CSR AI setup guidance](https://help.housecallpro.com/en/articles/12001958-csr-ai-best-practices-and-faqs).

sections.title: Use a workflow-choice card, not an invented ROI score
paragraphs:
Fill one card for each plausible task, then choose **one** for a bounded test. Use the [blank worksheet and fictional examples](workflow-choice-worksheet.md).

| Record on the card | What it establishes |
|---|---|
| Task and observed bottleneck | The specific work being considered, with evidence rather than a general desire to automate |
| Non-AI alternative | The existing template, form, report or manual process to compare against |
| Input source and version | Which facts or records are authoritative, and what is missing |
| Expected output and workflow type | Whether you need capture, a draft, analysis or an external action |
| Permitted action and human owner | What may happen without another approval, and who handles exceptions |
| Consequence of error | Who could be affected and whether the effect is reversible |
| Acceptance conditions and evidence | What the reviewer must observe before deciding the test is useful |
| Fallback and decision | How to stop safely; whether to test, revise or defer the task |

Do not total these fields into a universal “automation score.” A low-frequency action can still have a serious consequence. Select a workflow whose problem, inputs, reviewer and boundaries are all clear; defer one with unresolved authority or unreliable source data.

NIST's AI Risk Management Framework is voluntary guidance for considering risk in AI design, use and evaluation. The worksheet here is an editorial aid, not a NIST certification or a claim that a tool is risk-free. [NIST AI RMF](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework).

sections.title: Two offices can reasonably choose different first workflows
paragraphs:
### Office A: incomplete service requests

In this fictional example, a plumbing office repeatedly has to recover missing callback details. Its useful first experiment is **capture**, not autonomous scheduling. The expected output is a request containing the caller's stated need, a return number when supplied and clearly marked missing information.

The office manager owns review. The test cannot diagnose the problem, quote a repair price or promise a visit. A missing return number must stay missing, not be invented. This office defers its other candidate—automatic booking—because appointment-write authority and recovery are unresolved. The simpler alternative is a revised intake form or script. If that solves the capture problem, the office may not need an AI tool for it.

### Office B: repeated rewriting of approved descriptions

In this fictional example, a cleaning-business owner already has accurate descriptions but repeatedly rewrites them for different page lengths. The first experiment is **draft generation**. It does not require customer records, phone access or scheduling permissions.

The owner checks whether each draft preserves the approved services and exclusions. An added guarantee, price or service is a failure to correct, not creative improvement. The output stays unpublished until approved. This office defers its other candidate—AI analysis of request patterns—because its records do not yet distinguish new inquiries from repeat contacts. The simpler alternative for drafting is a reusable short-and-long description template.

Neither example establishes which task is best for every business. It shows why the initial decision should follow the work rather than a vendor's list of features.

sections.title: Test the choice without quietly expanding its authority
paragraphs:
Begin with fictional inputs or data you are authorized to use. Keep customer outreach, live record changes, payments and field-safety decisions outside this initial test. For conversation tools, use authorized test conversations rather than routing unsuspecting callers into an experiment.

Create four cases for the chosen task:

| Case | Capture example | Drafting example |
|---|---|---|
| Normal input | A stated service request with a callback number | A description containing the approved service and exclusions |
| Missing information | No callback number supplied | No approved price supplied |
| Outdated or conflicting source | Old service-area instructions conflict with the current version | An old description contains a guarantee absent from the current approved text |
| Outside the allowed scope | The caller asks for a diagnosis or a confirmed visit | The request asks the tool to publish the draft or invent a discount |

Keep the test proportionate. This is a task-selection exercise, not proof that a system is ready for unattended customer use. Once capture is the chosen workflow, the separate [receptionist selection guide](/ai-answering-service/choose-virtual-receptionist) covers provider requirements, and the [answering-service trial guide](/ai-answering-service/answering-service-free-trial) covers evaluating an offer.

sections.title: Decide whether to retain, revise or stop
paragraphs:
Compare the test with the manual or template-based alternative. Record output quality, correction effort, unresolved exceptions and the staff time actually observed. Include review and cleanup time; do not count only the seconds spent generating an answer. A small fictional test does not establish future revenue, time savings or accuracy rates.

- **Retain for further evaluation** when the bounded task meets the written acceptance conditions and the reviewer can verify its outputs. This is not authorization to add new actions.
- **Revise and retest** when a specific source, instruction or workflow problem can be corrected. Keep the same scope so the comparison remains meaningful.
- **Stop or defer** when authority is unclear, outputs cannot be checked or correction work defeats the purpose. Return to the stated manual process and review any pending work.

If call handling is the selected task, keep inquiries, bookings and completed jobs separate when measuring later results. A captured request is not a sold job. Use the existing [conversion measurement guide](/ai-answering-service/answering-service-conversion-rate-comparison) rather than treating every AI interaction as revenue.

sections.title: Where Revo fits
paragraphs:
Revo's published services include answering, lead intake and call summaries. If those match the task you selected, use the [current service description](https://www.revoapp.ai/services.html) to begin a configuration discussion. Confirm supported actions and plan scope before allowing booking or transfers. This guide does not present Revo as a general marketing-writing tool, business-analysis platform or autonomous field decision-maker.

The next step is small: complete one workflow-choice card and name its reviewer. If the card exposes a missing source or unclear authority, resolving that is progress—even when the right decision is not to automate yet.

title: Build vs buy an AI receptionist: costs and ownership
description: Compare a custom voice-agent build with a managed answering service by deciding who owns integrations, maintenance, incidents and the complete operating bill.
lead: A custom AI receptionist and a managed answering service can both answer a phone. The important buying difference is who is responsible for the system that turns that conversation into useful work—and who maintains it after the first demonstration.
intro: A custom AI receptionist and a managed answering service can both answer a phone. The important buying difference is who is responsible for the system that turns that conversation into useful work—and who maintains it after the first demonstration.

sections.title: Identify which arrangement you are actually considering
paragraphs:
There are at least three arrangements to distinguish in a proposal:

- **Managed answering service:** you contract for specified call-handling work. Confirm what the provider maintains and what remains with your staff.
- **Custom build on a developer platform:** your team assembles the business workflow using platform capabilities and any necessary integrations.
- **Agency-built solution:** a supplier builds the custom system, potentially on a third-party platform. Ongoing operation may or may not be included in the arrangement.

These are purchasing categories, not rigid labels applied to every seller. A platform can offer substantial support, and a managed service can still require configuration or office follow-up. Ask for named responsibilities rather than assuming that “managed” means your business has no remaining work.

Vapi, for example, explicitly positions itself for developers building voice applications. Its FAQ describes a modular voice pipeline and notes that advanced function calling requires a server URL that can receive and respond to messages. That is a different starting point from purchasing a defined receptionist workflow. [Vapi FAQ](https://docs.vapi.ai/faq)

sections.title: Specify the result before selecting the architecture
paragraphs:
Write down what must exist after a call. For a fictional service business, the required result might be an accurately captured inquiry at the right property, a confirmed booking only when authorized, and an owned callback task otherwise.

Describe exceptions too: an existing customer, an unsupported service request, an unavailable schedule and an unanswered transfer. Use the same requirements for each proposal. A custom build should not receive credit for a possible feature that has not been implemented; a managed service should not receive credit for a broad integration label without the necessary operation.

If the requirement is a live booking in a particular system, ask which operation writes that booking and how failure is reported. If a message is sufficient, do not add an elaborate integration solely because the platform supports one.

sections.title: Assign the operational responsibilities
paragraphs:
Use this proposed worksheet during the buying discussion. It is not a statement that a particular provider excludes any task.

| Responsibility | Evidence to request |
|---|---|
| Public number and routing | Account owner, authorized administrator and recovery procedure |
| Business instructions | Who approves changes and checks the active configuration |
| Custom integration | Maintainer, required access and supported operations |
| Credentials | Responsible owner and a documented update/revocation process |
| Monitoring | Who receives failures and determines whether customer work is affected |
| Changes | Who tests a new configuration before it handles customers |
| Incidents | Named responder, support scope and permitted fallback |
| Records and exit | Available exports, account access and outstanding-work handoff |

Do not leave a custom endpoint assigned to “the platform” if the vendor only hosts the voice layer. Equally, do not assume an agency has abandoned responsibility after setup: inspect the actual proposal and support arrangement.

Your business still owns its service policies. No implementation should invent a price, diagnose an equipment fault or promise a visit simply because a caller asks confidently.

sections.title: Compare the complete operating scope
paragraphs:
Vapi’s current billing documentation separates usage hosting from model, voice, transcriber and telephony costs. Success Packages, currently offered to new Vapi customers, add support and service commitments without replacing usage charges. It also notes that legacy customers retain their previous billing arrangements. Those details are specific to Vapi’s documented offer, not a universal billing formula for every platform. [Vapi pricing and Success Packages](https://docs.vapi.ai/billing/pricing-and-success-packages)

Ask for a like-for-like estimate that separates:

1. Initial implementation and configuration.
2. Recurring platform or service fees.
3. Usage components and the unit each one bills.
4. Required support or maintenance arrangements.
5. Hosting or other services used by custom integrations.
6. Your staff’s remaining review and correction work.

Use your own call pattern and a clearly labeled quieter/busier scenario. Include the same required coverage and tasks in every proposal. Do not treat a platform’s single component rate as a complete receptionist price or divide a managed plan’s allowance into an invented overage rate.

This guide does not provide a savings estimate or declare either approach cheaper. A lower technology bill may coexist with more maintenance work; a service subscription may cover useful work while leaving a specific requirement unsupported. Establish the scope first.

sections.title: Decide whether customization has an accountable owner
paragraphs:
A custom build can be worth evaluating when the business has a specific requirement that available managed offers do not meet and an accountable team to maintain it. For example, a fictional contractor may need a narrowly authorized interaction with an internal system that is not available through the shortlisted services.

The requirement is not complete merely because a demonstration can call that system once. Ask who will handle access changes, unavailable dependencies and an operation that appears to succeed during the conversation but leaves no valid office record.

A managed offer can be worth shortlisting when the supported workflow matches the business’s needs and the staff wants a defined operational handoff. That is not proof that all managed offers are suitable or that Revo supports the requirement. Verify the actual configuration and contract scope directly.

For an agency-built option, ask what happens when the original implementer is unavailable. Establish who controls the accounts, number, configuration and any custom code; who may authorize changes; and what documentation is handed over. Treat these as procurement questions for the responsible owners, not as assumptions about legal rights.

sections.title: Require evidence beyond a successful conversation
paragraphs:
Request an authorized sandbox or other non-live demonstration with fictional details. These are proposed evaluation steps; no calls, accounts or integrations were created for this guide.

- Inspect the resulting request or booking in the intended system.
- Demonstrate the agreed fallback when an integration is unavailable.
- Show how a business-rule update is reviewed and activated.
- Identify who receives the failure record and owns follow-up.
- Explain how the previous working route or configuration can be restored using supported controls.

A test can establish a specific observed result. It does not prove that every future call will work, that the provider meets an undocumented service level, or that a production rollout requires no further review.

sections.title: Make the decision from owned work
paragraphs:
Choose the approach whose supported outcome, maintenance obligation and full cost fit your business. If no one can explain who fixes a broken integration, the proposal is not ready. If a managed service cannot perform an essential action, its convenient package does not resolve that gap.

**Is building an AI receptionist the same as training an AI model?** Not necessarily. Configuring a voice application, instructions and tools does not by itself establish that the underlying model is being retrained.

**Does a developer platform mean there is no support?** No. Check the actual support tier and responsibilities. Vapi, for example, documents optional support packages; your own application maintenance remains a separate scope question.

# Build vs buy an AI receptionist: platform costs and operating ownership

**Description:** Compare a custom voice-agent build with a managed answering service by deciding who owns integrations, maintenance, incidents and the complete operating bill.

A custom AI receptionist and a managed answering service can both answer a phone. The important buying difference is who is responsible for the system that turns that conversation into useful work—and who maintains it after the first demonstration.

This is not an AI-versus-human comparison. Both approaches may use AI, and either may hand a call to a person. It is an ownership comparison for a business choosing between a defined service and a custom workflow built on a voice-agent platform.

Documentation was reviewed October 23, 2026. Product examples establish documented scope, not a performance ranking or a verified integration with Revo.

## Identify which arrangement you are actually considering

There are at least three arrangements to distinguish in a proposal:

- **Managed answering service:** you contract for specified call-handling work. Confirm what the provider maintains and what remains with your staff.
- **Custom build on a developer platform:** your team assembles the business workflow using platform capabilities and any necessary integrations.
- **Agency-built solution:** a supplier builds the custom system, potentially on a third-party platform. Ongoing operation may or may not be included in the arrangement.

These are purchasing categories, not rigid labels applied to every seller. A platform can offer substantial support, and a managed service can still require configuration or office follow-up. Ask for named responsibilities rather than assuming that “managed” means your business has no remaining work.

Vapi, for example, explicitly positions itself for developers building voice applications. Its FAQ describes a modular voice pipeline and notes that advanced function calling requires a server URL that can receive and respond to messages. That is a different starting point from purchasing a defined receptionist workflow. [Vapi FAQ](https://docs.vapi.ai/faq)

## Specify the result before selecting the architecture

Write down what must exist after a call. For a fictional service business, the required result might be an accurately captured inquiry at the right property, a confirmed booking only when authorized, and an owned callback task otherwise.

Describe exceptions too: an existing customer, an unsupported service request, an unavailable schedule and an unanswered transfer. Use the same requirements for each proposal. A custom build should not receive credit for a possible feature that has not been implemented; a managed service should not receive credit for a broad integration label without the necessary operation.

If the requirement is a live booking in a particular system, ask which operation writes that booking and how failure is reported. If a message is sufficient, do not add an elaborate integration solely because the platform supports one.

## Assign the operational responsibilities

Use this proposed worksheet during the buying discussion. It is not a statement that a particular provider excludes any task.

| Responsibility | Evidence to request |
|---|---|
| Public number and routing | Account owner, authorized administrator and recovery procedure |
| Business instructions | Who approves changes and checks the active configuration |
| Custom integration | Maintainer, required access and supported operations |
| Credentials | Responsible owner and a documented update/revocation process |
| Monitoring | Who receives failures and determines whether customer work is affected |
| Changes | Who tests a new configuration before it handles customers |
| Incidents | Named responder, support scope and permitted fallback |
| Records and exit | Available exports, account access and outstanding-work handoff |

Do not leave a custom endpoint assigned to “the platform” if the vendor only hosts the voice layer. Equally, do not assume an agency has abandoned responsibility after setup: inspect the actual proposal and support arrangement.

Your business still owns its service policies. No implementation should invent a price, diagnose an equipment fault or promise a visit simply because a caller asks confidently.

## Compare the complete operating scope

Vapi’s current billing documentation separates usage hosting from model, voice, transcriber and telephony costs. Success Packages, currently offered to new Vapi customers, add support and service commitments without replacing usage charges. It also notes that legacy customers retain their previous billing arrangements. Those details are specific to Vapi’s documented offer, not a universal billing formula for every platform. [Vapi pricing and Success Packages](https://docs.vapi.ai/billing/pricing-and-success-packages)

Ask for a like-for-like estimate that separates:

1. Initial implementation and configuration.
2. Recurring platform or service fees.
3. Usage components and the unit each one bills.
4. Required support or maintenance arrangements.
5. Hosting or other services used by custom integrations.
6. Your staff’s remaining review and correction work.

Use your own call pattern and a clearly labeled quieter/busier scenario. Include the same required coverage and tasks in every proposal. Do not treat a platform’s single component rate as a complete receptionist price or divide a managed plan’s allowance into an invented overage rate.

This guide does not provide a savings estimate or declare either approach cheaper. A lower technology bill may coexist with more maintenance work; a service subscription may cover useful work while leaving a specific requirement unsupported. Establish the scope first.

## Decide whether customization has an accountable owner

A custom build can be worth evaluating when the business has a specific requirement that available managed offers do not meet and an accountable team to maintain it. For example, a fictional contractor may need a narrowly authorized interaction with an internal system that is not available through the shortlisted services.

The requirement is not complete merely because a demonstration can call that system once. Ask who will handle access changes, unavailable dependencies and an operation that appears to succeed during the conversation but leaves no valid office record.

A managed offer can be worth shortlisting when the supported workflow matches the business’s needs and the staff wants a defined operational handoff. That is not proof that all managed offers are suitable or that Revo supports the requirement. Verify the actual configuration and contract scope directly.

For an agency-built option, ask what happens when the original implementer is unavailable. Establish who controls the accounts, number, configuration and any custom code; who may authorize changes; and what documentation is handed over. Treat these as procurement questions for the responsible owners, not as assumptions about legal rights.

## Require evidence beyond a successful conversation

Request an authorized sandbox or other non-live demonstration with fictional details. These are proposed evaluation steps; no calls, accounts or integrations were created for this guide.

- Inspect the resulting request or booking in the intended system.
- Demonstrate the agreed fallback when an integration is unavailable.
- Show how a business-rule update is reviewed and activated.
- Identify who receives the failure record and owns follow-up.
- Explain how the previous working route or configuration can be restored using supported controls.

A test can establish a specific observed result. It does not prove that every future call will work, that the provider meets an undocumented service level, or that a production rollout requires no further review.

## Make the decision from owned work

Choose the approach whose supported outcome, maintenance obligation and full cost fit your business. If no one can explain who fixes a broken integration, the proposal is not ready. If a managed service cannot perform an essential action, its convenient package does not resolve that gap.

**Is building an AI receptionist the same as training an AI model?** Not necessarily. Configuring a voice application, instructions and tools does not by itself establish that the underlying model is being retrained.

**Does a developer platform mean there is no support?** No. Check the actual support tier and responsibilities. Vapi, for example, documents optional support packages; your own application maintenance remains a separate scope question.

**Does Revo remove the need for every custom integration?** This guide makes no such claim. Confirm Revo’s current supported workflow before choosing it over a build.

For related decisions, use [answering-service costs](https://www.revoapp.ai/ai-answering-service/answering-service-cost), [choosing a virtual receptionist](https://www.revoapp.ai/ai-answering-service/choose-virtual-receptionist), and [home-service receptionist alternatives](https://www.revoapp.ai/ai-answering-service/compare/home-services-ai-receptionists). Check [Revo’s current plans](https://www.revoapp.ai/pricing.html) for the offer—not an assumed replacement for your requirements review.
