title: Posh Virtual Receptionist Reviews: A Buyer’s Checklist
description: Review Posh’s AI and live answering options, attributed customer feedback, billing questions and a practical checklist for home-service buyers.
intro: Looking at Posh virtual receptionist reviews? Separate the current offer, the experience reported by an individual customer and the workflow your business needs before choosing an answering service.
lead: Looking at Posh virtual receptionist reviews? Separate the current offer, the experience reported by an individual customer and the workflow your business needs before choosing an answering service.

sections.title: How this review was prepared
paragraphs:
Revo publishes this review and sells a competing AI answering service. We reviewed public Posh product information and selected customer reports on Trustpilot on October 27, 2026. We did not purchase Posh, place test calls or independently verify reviewers’ experiences. This is a documentary buying guide, without a Revo-assigned score or claim to independent product testing.

The useful question is whether the service can handle your particular calls at an acceptable cost. A favorable review from another business cannot settle your service-area rules, scheduling requirements or escalation instructions.

sections.title: What Posh currently offers
paragraphs:
[Posh’s current AI page](https://posh.com/ai/) describes a combination of AI answering and live receptionists. Callers can move from AI to a human, with transfer rules configured during setup. The page specifically discusses home-service lead qualification and human handling of escalations. Those are vendor descriptions, not performance results established by our review.

That distinction matters when comparing providers. Confirm who receives an escalated call: your employee, a provider’s receptionist or another destination. Do not treat those arrangements as interchangeable. If a human answering team is essential, request an explicit explanation of its availability and responsibilities.

sections.title: What selected customers reported
paragraphs:
The [Posh Trustpilot profile](https://www.trustpilot.com/review/posh.com) supplies identifiable examples, rather than proof of typical results. Rocky Mountain Exteriors, in a review posted June 6, 2025 about a May 24 experience, reported helpful after-hours handling and account support. The Professor Law Firm reported smooth setup on September 14, 2026; its legal-office context differs from a contractor’s dispatch workflow.

There is criticism too. Posh Event Center’s April 12, 2026 review, describing an October 25, 2025 experience, reported unexpectedly high costs and more calls reaching the business than anticipated, while valuing human answering. Posh replied that transfer attempts could relate to setup. That explanation is the vendor’s response, not an independently established cause.

Trustpilot labels these reports Verified. We have not authenticated them ourselves. These selected accounts are not a representative sample or a customer consensus, and older live-service experiences do not prove the quality of today’s AI offering.

sections.title: Read the billing units before comparing monthly prices
paragraphs:
Posh’s AI page describes plans with a shared allowance of AI and live receptionist minutes, followed by different overage rates for each. Its billing explanation also includes immediate follow-up tasks. A call that uses AI and then a human can incur both types of overage after the allowance is exhausted. Check the current terms directly before buying.

Build a scenario from your own records instead of comparing starting prices alone. Use a typical month and a busy month. Write down answered-call minutes, minutes transferred to humans, follow-up work and any other quoted charges. Ask the provider to calculate both scenarios in writing and explain how usage appears on the invoice.

sections.title: Use this call-handling worksheet in your evaluation
paragraphs:
Copy these five scenarios into your evaluation notes. For each, record the expected action, actual result, minutes used and correction needed:

1. **New customer outside your service area.** Supply a ZIP code you do not serve. The expected result is an accurate explanation and your chosen next step, without an unsupported appointment promise.
2. **Routine appointment request.** Give a real type of job but use a fictional caller. Record whether the result is a message, appointment request or confirmed booking, and what makes that status clear.
3. **Existing customer asking for an update.** Specify what information the answering service may access and what must go to your office. Check that it does not guess an arrival time.
4. **Caller requesting a person.** Document the handoff destination, hours, information passed along and fallback when nobody answers. Include the cost of that path.
5. **Urgent-sounding request after hours.** Use a hypothetical scenario agreed with the provider. Check your escalation instructions and fallback; do not assume an answering service replaces emergency services.

Use the same scenarios for every shortlisted service. Arrange a demonstration or controlled evaluation with permission, rather than sending fake emergencies through a live customer queue. Keep personal customer information out of evaluation material.

sections.title: Questions to settle before you choose
paragraphs:
Ask who maintains your instructions and how quickly changes take effect. Establish how you report an incorrect message or transfer and how the provider confirms the correction. Request the cancellation terms and treatment of unused allowances. Decide which failures would stop the evaluation: an appointment promised without authorization, an incorrect service-area decision or an escalation sent to the wrong person.

Posh merits consideration when you want to evaluate a documented AI-plus-human model. Your decision should rest on the agreed call flow, observed evaluation results and written costs. If you are also considering Revo, compare its documented plan scope separately; this guide does not establish equivalent human staffing or transfer arrangements.

Review its published scope alongside your other options.

faqs.q: Do Posh reviews establish how its AI receptionist performs?
faqs.a: Not by themselves. A report may concern live answering, onboarding or an older configuration. Ask which service was used and evaluate the current call flow against your own requirements.

faqs.q: What should a home-service business compare first?
faqs.a: Start with intake accuracy, booking authority and escalation destination. Then price the same typical and busy-month scenarios across providers.

takeaway: Compare Revo plans

sections.title: Ask the provider to complete this scope card
paragraphs:
Use one card for each offer. Leave an unanswered item marked unknown rather than treating it as included.

| Item | What to record in the quote |
|---|---|
| Unlimited quantity | Calls, minutes, users or another expressly defined unit |
| Included work | Answering, intake, booking, transfers and any separately charged activity |
| Eligibility | Covered numbers, locations, callers, hours and permitted business use |
| Fair use | Thresholds, prohibited activity, review process and possible service changes |
| Concurrent calls | Documented account capacity and the next caller's outcome |
| Outside scope | Extra charges, restricted tasks and the office work that remains |
| Evidence | Current terms, date, selected plan and person confirming unresolved details |

This card is a purchasing worksheet, not a description of a particular provider's terms. An offer may have no limit in one row and a material restriction in another.

sections.title: Read unlimited in the context of the service model
paragraphs:
Specialty Answering Service uses the phrase unlimited answering service in its description of dedicated virtual agents. That establishes that the provider markets an arrangement using the term; it does not establish that every SAS product, task or account has no restrictions. Read the selected offer and its agreement instead of carrying that phrase across the provider's entire catalog. [SAS virtual assistants](https://www.specialtyansweringservice.net/virtual-office/virtual-assistants/)

An allowance-based AI receptionist, a shared human answering team and a dedicated staffing arrangement can allocate work differently. Ask who answers, what happens when that person or system cannot complete a request, and who maintains the instructions. Do not assume the same service merely because two offers use the word answering.

sections.title: Separate a busy month from a busy moment
paragraphs:
A monthly usage promise concerns the period's total activity. Concurrency concerns calls that overlap. For example, two homeowners might call while another conversation is still underway. Ask what happens to each caller and to a transfer back to your office. Unlimited monthly usage does not answer those questions.

Use the [simultaneous-call capacity guide](/ai-answering-service/simultaneous-call-capacity) for the separate capacity review. Do not conduct a load test without the providers' authorization. A successful demonstration at an agreed load is an observation, not proof of limitless capacity.

sections.title: Compare the work that stays with your office
paragraphs:
Use three fictional requests in a provider-approved demonstration: a new customer asking for an appointment, an existing customer requesting a change, and a caller needing a person who is unavailable. Ask the provider to show the resulting record and the next responsible person. No real customer information is needed.

If a booking cannot be confirmed, the result should remain a request for review. If a transfer fails, identify the agreed fallback. An unlimited conversation allowance cannot substitute for a usable next step. For the billing comparison itself, use the [answering-service cost guide](/ai-answering-service/answering-service-cost); for minimum commitments and usage charging, see [pay-as-you-go answering](/ai-answering-service/pay-as-you-go-answering-service).

sections.title: Where Revo fits
paragraphs:
Revo's published plans use included minutes: Solo 100, Crew 200 and Fleet 400. They are not presented here as unlimited plans. Its pricing page lists 24/7 answering, your script, hours and rules, appointment booking and call summaries. Team transfers are listed for Crew and Fleet, not Solo. Confirm the supported booking and handoff configuration for your business. [Current Revo plans](https://www.revoapp.ai/pricing)

Choose on required scope and documented terms. A business with predictable usage may prefer an allowance; another may need to investigate a different arrangement. This guide does not establish which is cheaper or better for your calls.

sections.title: Questions before you buy
paragraphs:
**Does unlimited mean no extra charges?** Not by itself. Ask which activities, numbers and services are included and obtain the terms for everything outside that scope.

**Does unlimited mean every caller connects immediately?** No conclusion about simultaneous capacity follows from a monthly usage label. Resolve capacity and fallback separately.

**Is Revo unlimited?** Revo publishes plans with included minutes. Review the current offer and applicable usage terms instead of assuming unlimited use or calculating an extra-minute rate from the subscription price.

**Next step:** [Review Revo's plans](https://www.revoapp.ai/pricing) and bring the completed scope card to a coverage discussion. Ask which of your required call tasks the selected setup can demonstrate.

intro: A homeowner asking about new flooring may be ready for a measurement visit, still choosing materials or calling about an estimate your office already issued. Those are different next steps. sections.title: Separate the measurement request from the installation commitment
paragraphs:
Before using an answering service, decide whether the next appointment is a site measurement, an office or showroom consultation, or a follow-up discussion about an existing estimate. An opening in one appointment type does not establish availability for another.

sections.title: Use this measurement-request and follow-up register
paragraphs:

| Record | What reception can capture under your instructions | Office check before committing |
|---|---|---|

sections.title: Give an existing estimate a different next step
paragraphs:
A caller who already has a quote should not automatically receive another initial measurement appointment. Capture the reference and the question: are they asking to discuss the material, understand the proposed work, revisit the timing or request a change? The office should locate the applicable estimate and decide whether a new visit is necessary.

paragraphs: This page concerns installation or replacement intake and the preparation of a measurement request. title: AI receptionist return on investment: a net-value worksheet
description: Evaluate an AI receptionist using incremental job contribution, full service costs and a baseline. Use a worksheet without assuming every call becomes revenue.
lead: An AI receptionist return on investment calculation should answer one question: does the extra value you can fairly attribute to the service exceed its full cost? Answered calls and gross job value are signals, not the return.
intro: An AI receptionist return on investment calculation should answer one question: does the extra value you can fairly attribute to the service exceed its full cost? Answered calls and gross job value are signals, not the return.

sections.title: Choose the alternative you are comparing
paragraphs: Describe what happens without the purchase, including callbacks your team already makes. A caller who would have booked after a callback is not an extra job created by the service.

sections.title: Build the worksheet from five entries
paragraphs:
Use one period for every entry and note the source or assumption beside each one.
- **A. Extra job contribution:** additional completed work minus the job costs it adds (parts, labor, travel).
- **B. Avoided expense:** a cash cost that actually disappears.
- **C. Recurring service cost:** subscription + expected usage + required add-ons.
- **D. Retained operating cost:** paid time for review, corrections and handoffs.
- **E. One-time launch cost:** setup and paid implementation work.

sections.title: Run the three steps
paragraphs:
1. Recurring net benefit = A + B − C − D.
2. First-period net benefit = recurring net benefit − E.
3. First-period return = first-period net benefit ÷ (C + D + E), only when that total is above zero.

If recurring net benefit is zero or negative, there is no payback period under those assumptions. Also run a lower-demand case.

Record owner time freed from the phones separately unless it produces a real cash saving, and never count it twice.

sections.title: Start with Phone, then examine the larger product separately
paragraphs:
Beside's current site distinguishes the available Beside Phone product from its broader business-agent offering. Start with the [Phone product page](https://www.beside.com/phone) and its plan page. Write the exact product, purchase channel, billing unit and included reception allowance on your comparison sheet. sections.title: Identify the offer available to your signup route
paragraphs:
Beside's [Phone pricing page](https://www.beside.com/phone/pricing) lists web plans billed monthly per business and separately describes some mobile subscriptions billed per seat. It also distinguishes the AI-receptionist allowance from ordinary calling and texting. Those are material differences; a general “unlimited calls” phrase does not tell you the reception allowance for every offer.

The purchase screen and applicable terms should settle the offer for your account, country and signup channel. Record whether a trial is offered, when billing starts and where cancellation is managed. A free app download is not evidence of free ongoing reception. This guide does not combine a web allowance with a mobile subscription price or assume an existing account receives a newly advertised plan.

sections.title: Build a decision record around your actual business line
paragraphs:
Copy the table below for each option. Complete the evidence column from the provider's applicable plan and a demonstration using fictional caller details. Unresolved items should stay unresolved until the supplier confirms them.

| Decision | Evidence to obtain | Office action before starting |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Number arrangement | New number, forwarding or porting route supported for this account | Identify who controls the existing number and approves changes |
| Calls the AI answers | Primary answering, missed-call coverage or another configured rule | Define the intended ringing and fallback behavior |
| Reception allowance | What counts as an AI-handled call and what happens at the allowance | Compare against your own eligible call mix |
| Booking outcome | Supported calendar, approved availability and confirmation behavior | Separate a confirmed slot from a requested time |
| Human handoff | Supported destination, plan and unavailable-contact outcome | Name the person responsible for exceptions |
| Account ownership | Billing administrator, team access and purchase channel | Keep business ownership clear if staff change |
| End of service | Number arrangements, supported exports and cancellation process | Document a handback plan before changing a live line |

sections.title: Separate the buying requirements before comparing providers
paragraphs:
Answer United's [propane answering page](https://www.answerunited.com/propane-answering-service/) describes delivery requests and general customer support alongside emergencies. [Ambs](https://www.ambscallcenter.com/propane-answering-service/) describes will-call and keep-full customers as well as emergency dispatch. These are descriptions of those providers' offers, not functions verified for Revo.

That mix matters when reviewing a proposal. A service that reliably receives ordinary requests is not automatically suitable for safety-critical calls. If emergency coverage is essential, require evidence for the specific trained response, escalation and acknowledgement process you need. Do not replace an established emergency route with general AI intake on the strength of a broad answering-service label.

sections.title: Give routine requests a usable office record
paragraphs:
For routine residential delivery inquiries, distinguish the service location from the billing address. A caller may manage more than one property or contact you about a tank at a different address. Use an account or tank reference only when the caller supplies it and your approved process allows it; collecting a reference does not authenticate the caller or verify account status.

Ask what the caller wants your office to review. A will-call delivery request, a question about an existing automatic-delivery arrangement and a new-customer inquiry leave different work for staff. sections.title: Use this routine-call scope card
paragraphs:
Complete the card with your own approved instructions and the provider's demonstrated scope. It is a reusable purchasing resource, not a claim that a particular system performs the listed actions.

| Routine request | Context the office may need | Decision retained by the business |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New residential account inquiry | Service address, callback details and requested next step | Service availability, eligibility and account opening |
| Will-call delivery request | Account reference if supplied, delivery address and requested timing | Order acceptance, quantity, pricing and route assignment |
| Automatic-delivery question | Caller-described arrangement and the question being raised | Confirmation of program status and any change |
| Existing delivery follow-up | Customer reference and the information requested | Actual order status and any confirmed delivery update |
| Address discrepancy | Addresses as stated and which location needs service | Record correction after the approved verification process |
| Access or site question | Caller-supplied description and contact person | Whether the site can be served and what conditions apply |
| Invoice or account question | The question and an approved callback route | Account investigation, payment handling and adjustments |
| Unclear or excluded request | The caller's words and the approved next contact | Specialist review; no invented answer or commitment |

Do not use the card to gather payment credentials or decide a technical or safety question. Define what information may be collected, who may see it and which matters require your existing specialist process.

sections.title: A requested delivery is not a dispatched truck
paragraphs:
Use clear outcome language in the proposed workflow. “Your delivery request has been recorded for the office to review” means something different from “Your delivery is confirmed.” The latter requires actual authority and current information. A preferred day does not reserve route capacity, establish tank access or confirm a price.

During an evaluation, use a fictional request that includes a different billing and delivery address. Ask to see the resulting message or supported record. sections.title: Maintain the specialist route alongside routine coverage
paragraphs:
A distributor may already publish separate contact instructions. For example, [Independent Propane's contact page](https://www.ipropane.com/contact-us/) identifies an emergency after-hours answering service separately from its office details. That is evidence of a distinct operating requirement, not a universal configuration or a recommendation to copy another company's response instructions.

Before activation, have the responsible business personnel confirm which calls the proposed routine flow may receive, which it must not attempt to resolve and how the existing specialist contact path is preserved. Obtain the provider's supported behavior in writing. This guide does not prescribe gas-leak instructions, certify a response process or claim Revo can recognize and safely manage every emergency description.

sections.title: Compare Revo for the narrower task it can support
paragraphs:
Revo publishes AI answering, intake, appointment booking and summaries, with team transfers and other features dependent on the selected plan and supported configuration. For a fuel distributor, evaluate whether a proposed routine intake and office handoff is sufficient. Do not assume a named fuel-software integration, delivery-order write, dispatch acknowledgement or emergency response capability.

Bring your routine scope card to the comparison and review [current Revo plans](/pricing). If the purchase depends on an unverified specialist function, resolve that requirement before choosing the service. A routine receptionist should complement an established operating process, not silently take responsibility for the entire fuel-delivery business.

sections.title: Frequently asked questions
paragraphs:
### Does this guide recommend Revo for propane emergencies?

No. Emergency gas-call handling and safety assessment have not been established here. Keep specialist response requirements separate and verify them with the responsible provider and business personnel.

### Can recording a will-call request confirm a delivery?

No. Recording the customer's request does not establish order acceptance, route availability, dispatch, quantity or price.

### Should propane and heating-oil answering have separate buying guides?

The routine office decisions overlap: identify the customer and service location, preserve the request and retain delivery commitments with the distributor. Confirm fuel-specific procedures within that shared purchasing framework.

### Can an answering flow read our fuel-management system?

Only if the particular connection and permitted actions are verified for your setup. This article establishes no such Revo integration.

[Compare Revo's current answering plans](/pricing) against your documented routine-call scope and specialist requirements.

title: Virtual receptionist vs virtual assistant: choose the work
description: Compare virtual receptionist and virtual assistant scope for a service business. Decide between phone coverage and assigned administrative work before buying.
lead: A virtual receptionist and a virtual assistant may both answer a phone, but buying either label does not define the work you will receive. A home-service business choosing between them should separate availability for incoming conversations from time and responsibility assigned to administrative tasks. The useful choice depends on which work is currently unfinished.
intro: A virtual receptionist and a virtual assistant may both answer a phone, but buying either label does not define the work you will receive. A home-service business choosing between them should separate availability for incoming conversations from time and responsibility assigned to administrative tasks. The useful choice depends on which work is currently unfinished.

sections.title: Diagnose the gap before choosing the role
paragraphs:
Consider two fictional problems in a residential service office. During installations, new callers cannot reach anyone to explain what they need. Separately, the owner has a list of estimates awaiting a staff decision, supplier emails to organize and documents to prepare for tomorrow. Those problems may occur together, but they do not become one purchasing requirement merely because both interrupt the owner.

The first problem calls for defined reception coverage and a reliable office handoff. The second calls for administrative capacity, access and an agreed completion standard. A provider can potentially sell both, but the proposal should say so explicitly. Do not infer continuing desk work from a call-answering allowance, or continuous phone availability from a block of assistant hours.

sections.title: Define coverage and assigned work separately
paragraphs:
For reception, describe when a caller needs an answer and what may happen during that conversation: approved questions, request capture, supported booking or a handoff. Ask what happens when the request falls outside those instructions. Coverage is useful even when the office retains the final decision.

For administrative assistance, describe a task with a start, required inputs and an observable finish. “Organize supplier messages into the approved job folders by Thursday” is more reviewable than “help with admin.” State which decisions the assistant may make, what needs approval and who handles questions when the owner is unavailable.

Neither definition determines whether the work is performed by a person or AI. Product labels and staffing models vary. Use the separate [AI-versus-live-receptionist comparison](/ai-answering-service/compare/ai-vs-live-receptionist) when the question is how calls are handled. Here, the decision is the work being purchased.

sections.title: Complete a two-part purchase brief
paragraphs:
Copy these two cards and fill them before requesting proposals. They are designed to expose a missing responsibility rather than rank providers by a broad label.

**Reception coverage card**

- Coverage window: ______
- Incoming call types included: ______
- Information or approved answers required: ______
- Supported booking or transfer outcome: ______
- Outcome when the office cannot be reached: ______
- Usage unit, allowance and excluded work: ______
- Business owner who maintains the instructions: ______

**Administrative assignment card**

- Specific recurring assignment: ______
- Required inputs and approved access: ______
- Deliverable and completion deadline: ______
- Decisions permitted without further approval: ______
- Decisions reserved for the business: ______
- Time allocation, priority changes and unfinished-work process: ______
- Person who reviews completion and provides absence cover: ______

If a supplier offers both roles, ask it to complete both cards. Do not allocate the same paid hour to uninterrupted administrative work and continuous call coverage without confirming how interruptions and priorities are managed.

sections.title: Test ownership with one unfinished estimate
paragraphs:
An estimate has already been issued, and the customer calls to ask whether a different material changes the proposal. Reception can record the request and direct it to the authorized estimator. That does not revise the estimate or approve a new price.

An administrative assignment could be to assemble the customer's question and existing documents for the estimator, then record the approved decision in the agreed place. Whether an assistant can do that depends on access, instructions and the actual contract. The supplier should demonstrate the assignment rather than rely on a generic promise to manage your business.

If the need includes contacting the customer later, verify who is authorized to do so and the applicable process. Revo outbound calling, estimate revision and independent sales follow-through are not established by this guide. An inbound answering feature should not be presented as proof of those functions.

sections.title: Compare the cost of the defined work
paragraphs:
Ask a receptionist supplier how calls, minutes, coverage and additional tasks are billed. Ask an assistant supplier how time, availability, supervision and task changes are scoped. Keep provider charges separate from retained office work: reviewing uncertain requests, approving commercial decisions and maintaining instructions.

A lower quoted price is not a complete comparison if one offer covers incoming calls and another includes administrative assignments. Equally, buying broader support can be unnecessary when the actual gap is answering and capturing a routine request. No salary, hourly-rate benchmark or promised savings is supplied here; use current proposals for the same written scope.

sections.title: Where Revo fits in the decision
paragraphs:
Revo publishes AI answering, intake, appointment booking and call summaries; team transfers and other features depend on the selected plan and supported configuration. Evaluate it when the purchase is a supported incoming-call workflow. Review [current Revo plans](/pricing) against the reception coverage card.

This article does not claim that Revo supplies a human virtual assistant, manages email or supplier documents, prepares estimates, operates arbitrary business software or owns a continuing administrative assignment. If those tasks are essential, obtain a separate verified arrangement. An office can use reception and administrative support together when responsibility for the handoff is explicit.

sections.title: Frequently asked questions
paragraphs:
### Can a virtual assistant also answer calls?

Possibly. Confirm the actual coverage hours, interruptions, call tools and contract. The title alone does not establish continuous reception availability.

### Can a virtual receptionist perform administrative work?

Some suppliers may include additional tasks. Ask for a named deliverable, permitted access and completion responsibility rather than assuming every call-answering offer includes them.

### Is this the same decision as AI versus a human receptionist?

No. AI versus human concerns the handling model. Reception versus assistance concerns incoming-call coverage and assigned work. Evaluate both questions separately when relevant.

### Which should a small contractor buy first?

Identify the unfinished work using the two purchase cards. If callers cannot reach you, evaluate coverage. If requests are captured but administrative assignments remain unfinished, specify that work and verify a supplier's scope. This guide does not prescribe the same answer for every business.

[Review Revo's answering plans](/pricing) for the reception portion of your purchase brief, and keep administrative assignments explicit.

sections.title: Start with Horizon's contractor offer
paragraphs:

sections.title: Build a coverage map for the actual office
paragraphs:

| Office requirement | Evidence to obtain | Responsibility to keep explicit |

| New residential inquiry | Included hours, accepted request details and resulting record | Who confirms service fit and next steps |
| Existing-job question | Reference information and destination for the question | Who knows the actual job status |
| Employee needs a message | Delivery channel and information included | Who reads it and owns follow-up |
| A request needs escalation | The agreed recipient and contact sequence | Who acknowledges receipt and makes the business decision |

title: In-house receptionist vs answering service: who owns the work?
description: Compare hiring a receptionist with buying answering coverage. Map physical duties, supervision, absences and retained office work before comparing costs.
lead: For a home-service business, hiring a receptionist buys an employee's assigned working time. Buying an answering service buys an agreed call-handling scope. The decision starts with the rest of the job, not with a claim that one monthly fee replaces a whole employee.
intro: For a home-service business, hiring a receptionist buys an employee's assigned working time. Buying an answering service buys an agreed call-handling scope. The decision starts with the rest of the job, not with a claim that one monthly fee replaces a whole employee.

sections.title: Divide the position into work that can and cannot move
paragraphs:
Use this worksheet with the person who currently runs the office. Assign a real owner to every duty; leave a gap visible when neither proposal covers it.

| Duty | Employee arrangement | Answering-service arrangement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Receive routine new-job calls | Hours, queue and backup to define | Included coverage and intake outcome to verify |
| Greet visitors or accept deliveries | On-site assignment to define | Keep with an available person |
| Coordinate a changed job with a technician | Access, authority and manager to define | Identify what can be captured versus what needs your team |
| Prepare paperwork or reconcile records | Time and systems to allocate | Retained unless specifically purchased and verified |
| Cover lunch, leave or an unexpected absence | Backup employee or separate arrangement | Check contracted hours and exceptions |
| Supervise quality and update instructions | Manager still needed | Business instruction owner still needed |

A fictional plumbing office might need someone at the counter for parts deliveries as well as on the phone. Outsourcing routine calls does not receive the delivery. Conversely, assigning calls to an employee does not by itself establish coverage when that employee is away.

sections.title: Compare employment responsibility with supplier responsibility
paragraphs:
An employee proposal needs a job description, recruitment and training plan, supervisor, equipment and absence coverage. Obtain applicable payroll and employment guidance for your circumstances rather than treating a national salary estimate as your loaded cost.

A supplier proposal needs an included task, hours, billing definition, instruction-maintenance process and recipient for exceptions. Its cost comparison must include the work your office continues to perform. If the owner still returns every detailed job question, keep that time in the model.

Use: employee arrangement cost plus its uncovered work, versus service charges plus retained office work and any separate coverage. Fill the inputs with your actual quotes and working records. This is a decision structure, not a promised savings calculation.

sections.title: Choose a mixed arrangement when the position requires one
paragraphs:
The answer need not be a total replacement. A receptionist may retain the counter, paperwork and complex coordination while an answering provider handles an agreed overflow window. Specify who answers first and who owns an unresolved request. Test the proposed handoff with fictional calls before sending customer traffic.

sections.title: Locate the autonomous incoming-call offer
paragraphs:

sections.title: Request an outcome map for your trade office
paragraphs:

| --- | --- | --- |

paragraphs:

Inspect which information is captured and whether a real supported scheduling action establishes that time. If it does not, the result should remain a request for the authorized office rather than an invented confirmed visit.

Dialpad's examples of urgent routing do not establish your safety assessment or field dispatch process. Define those requirements with the supplier and your responsible team. Do not carry an unverified emergency or technical capability into a comparison with another provider.

title: AI receptionist call summaries: compare the office handoff
description: Compare AI receptionist summary controls, delivery and source records. Use a practical call packet to check what your office actually receives.
lead: The best summary for your service office is the one that leaves your team with an understandable request and a clear next action. Before buying an AI receptionist, compare the actual output, its destination and the source material available when a detail is uncertain. A notification arriving does not establish that someone accepted the work.
intro: The best summary for your service office is the one that leaves your team with an understandable request and a clear next action. Before buying an AI receptionist, compare the actual output, its destination and the source material available when a detail is uncertain. A notification arriving does not establish that someone accepted the work.

sections.title: Compare controls, not the word “summary”
paragraphs:
[Upfirst's feature page](https://upfirst.ai/features/call-summaries) describes text and email delivery, multiple recipients and rules based on call type. Its [help article](https://help.upfirst.ai/en/articles/16004053-how-to-customize-your-call-summaries) documents configurable highlights. A highlight extracts information if it arises; it does not instruct the receptionist to ask a question. Changes apply to future calls, and a text may not fit every field.

[Abby's AI product page](https://www.abby.com/products/ai-receptionist/) describes summaries, transcripts and recordings through AbbyGO and its web portal, with text and email notifications. Confirm the applicable product, plan and notification contents rather than assuming every channel contains the complete record.

[Revo's pricing](https://www.revoapp.ai/pricing) lists a call dashboard with summaries in Solo, Crew and Fleet. Recordings and transcripts are excluded from Solo and included in Crew and Fleet. This guide does not establish custom summary fields, email-routing rules, export, retention periods or automated callback assignment for Revo.

| Product and documented approach | Buying distinction | What remains to verify for your account |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Upfirst: recipient and delivery rules; configurable highlights | Information extracted, questions asked and notification contents are separate controls | Selected plan, required fields, recipients and the actual short-text result |
| Abby AI: summary and source artifacts in app/portal, plus advertised notifications | The alert and the full call record may serve different office tasks | Exact entitlement, access and contents delivered through each chosen channel |
| Revo: dashboard summaries; recordings/transcripts in Crew and Fleet | Decide whether your team needs a summary alone or access to those additional artifacts | Supported workflow and selected plan; any requirement beyond the published scope |

These are documented distinctions, not observed comparisons of reliability. A supplier's description is a starting point for an account-specific demonstration.

sections.title: Bring the same fictional call packet to every demonstration
paragraphs:
Create two ordinary residential-service scenarios. The first caller requests a replacement estimate and gives a preferred day. The second is an existing customer asking to change an arranged visit. Neither scenario should include a real customer's details.

For the estimate, decide in advance which facts the office needs: requested service, service address, callback information and whether a visit was requested or actually booked. For the change, specify the existing appointment reference and what the caller wants changed. The receptionist must not turn a preference into a commitment your business has not authorized.

Use the same scenarios for each supplier. Ask to see the notification and the full record, not just a polished sample chosen for an unrelated industry. If the supplier cannot demonstrate a requirement, leave it unresolved rather than scoring it as included.

| Proposed check | Office requirement | Supplier demonstration result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Estimate status | Distinguish requested date from confirmed booking | Leave blank until demonstrated |
| Existing visit | Identify the original visit and requested change | Leave blank until demonstrated |
| Callback detail | Preserve the information the office needs to respond | Leave blank until demonstrated |
| Unclear information | Make uncertainty visible and identify available source evidence | Leave blank until demonstrated |
| Notification | Show what the intended recipient actually sees | Leave blank until demonstrated |
| Follow-up owner | Establish the office role responsible for reviewing and acting | Record your own agreed procedure |

The final row is deliberately an operating decision. A service can deliver a useful record while the office still needs a person to review it. Do not treat a sent notification, opened message and completed callback as interchangeable events.

sections.title: Evaluate a short alert and a full record separately
paragraphs:
A short message may help a technician notice that the office needs attention. The person reviewing an estimate may need more context. Compare those tasks separately so an attractive notification does not hide an incomplete record.

Ask what happens when a caller corrects a phone number or changes their requested date during the conversation. The proposed demonstration should reveal whether the final output preserves the correction and labels any unresolved detail. This is a purchasing check to perform, not a claim about how any supplier performed in our testing.

Decide which person may consult additional source material and who can correct an office record. If your requirement includes a particular export, retention period, permission model or connection, obtain that exact scope in writing. Its absence from this comparison is not evidence that every supplier offers it.

sections.title: Choose the smallest verified scope that completes the handoff
paragraphs:
For an office that reviews requests in a dashboard, Revo's published summaries may be relevant. If the office also needs recordings and transcripts, compare the applicable Crew or Fleet offer. If conditional email recipients or configurable highlights are mandatory, examine a supplier that documents them and verify the selected arrangement.

Keep pricing and supported reception tasks in the decision alongside the summary. A detailed record does not compensate for unsupported booking behavior, and a larger feature list does not establish that your team needs every feature.

sections.title: Frequently asked questions
paragraphs:
### Does a summary replace the recording or transcript?

They are different artifacts. Decide whether the summary alone supplies the information your office needs and which plan provides additional evidence if required.

### Does adding a summary field make the receptionist ask that question?

Do not assume it. Upfirst explicitly distinguishes extracting a highlight from adding a question to the receptionist's instructions. Confirm the relevant controls with each supplier.

### Is this a measured ranking of the best AI receptionist?

No. It is a documentary comparison and a reusable demonstration packet. No service-use test, accuracy score or customer outcome is reported.

[Compare Revo's current plans](/pricing) against the completed packet and the summary workflow your office can actually support.

takeaway: Compare Revo's current plans against the completed packet and the summary workflow your office can actually support.

| Upfirst: recipient and delivery rules; configurable highlights | Information extracted, questions asked and notification contents are separate controls | Selected plan, required fields, recipients and the actual short-text result |
| Abby AI: summary and source artifacts in app/portal, plus advertised notifications | The alert and the full call record may serve different office tasks | Exact entitlement, access and contents delivered through each chosen channel |
| Revo: dashboard summaries; recordings/transcripts in Crew and Fleet | Decide whether your team needs a summary alone or access to those additional artifacts | Supported workflow and selected plan; any requirement beyond the published scope |

These are documented distinctions, not observed comparisons of reliability. A supplier's description is a starting point for an account-specific demonstration.

## Bring the same fictional call packet to every demonstration

Create two ordinary residential-service scenarios. The first caller requests a replacement estimate and gives a preferred day. The second is an existing customer asking to change an arranged visit. Neither scenario should include a real customer's details.

For the estimate, decide in advance which facts the office needs: requested service, service address, callback information and whether a visit was requested or actually booked. For the change, specify the existing appointment reference and what the caller wants changed. The receptionist must not turn a preference into a commitment your business has not authorized.

Use the same scenarios for each supplier. Ask to see the notification and the full record, not just a polished sample chosen for an unrelated industry. If the supplier cannot demonstrate a requirement, leave it unresolved rather than scoring it as included.

| Proposed check | Office requirement | Supplier demonstration result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Estimate status | Distinguish requested date from confirmed booking | Leave blank until demonstrated |
| Existing visit | Identify the original visit and requested change | Leave blank until demonstrated |
| Callback detail | Preserve the information the office needs to respond | Leave blank until demonstrated |
| Unclear information | Make uncertainty visible and identify available source evidence | Leave blank until demonstrated |
| Notification | Show what the intended recipient actually sees | Leave blank until demonstrated |
| Follow-up owner | Establish the office role responsible for reviewing and acting | Record your own agreed procedure |

The final row is deliberately an operating decision. A service can deliver a useful record while the office still needs a person to review it. Do not treat a sent notification, opened message and completed callback as interchangeable events.

## Evaluate a short alert and a full record separately

A short message may help a technician notice that the office needs attention. The person reviewing an estimate may need more context. Compare those tasks separately so an attractive notification does not hide an incomplete record.

Ask what happens when a caller corrects a phone number or changes their requested date during the conversation. The proposed demonstration should reveal whether the final output preserves the correction and labels any unresolved detail. This is a purchasing check to perform, not a claim about how any supplier performed in our testing.

Decide which person may consult additional source material and who can correct an office record. If your requirement includes a particular export, retention period, permission model or connection, obtain that exact scope in writing. Its absence from this comparison is not evidence that every supplier offers it.

## Choose the smallest verified scope that completes the handoff

For an office that reviews requests in a dashboard, Revo's published summaries may be relevant. If the office also needs recordings and transcripts, compare the applicable Crew or Fleet offer. If conditional email recipients or configurable highlights are mandatory, examine a supplier that documents them and verify the selected arrangement.

Keep pricing and supported reception tasks in the decision alongside the summary. A detailed record does not compensate for unsupported booking behavior, and a larger feature list does not establish that your team needs every feature.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does a summary replace the recording or transcript?

They are different artifacts. Decide whether the summary alone supplies the information your office needs and which plan provides additional evidence if required.

### Does adding a summary field make the receptionist ask that question?

Do not assume it. Upfirst explicitly distinguishes extracting a highlight from adding a question to the receptionist's instructions. Confirm the relevant controls with each supplier.

No. It is a documentary comparison and a reusable demonstration packet. No service-use test, accuracy score or customer outcome is reported.

sections.title: Start with the actual AnswerUSA choices
paragraphs:
The [AnswerUSA homepage](https://answerusa.com/) presents Flex without minimums or commitment to monthly minute plans. It separately names Starter, Business and Executive, each directing the buyer to obtain a quote. The page establishes a US staffed service and explicitly serves contractors.

The reviewed offer supplies no complete numerical tariff or allowance for comparing those routes. Do not invent a cheapest plan, read a volume threshold into “Business,” or assume “Executive” includes a particular software action. Flex's wording does not establish that every activity is free of charges or that there is no service agreement.

sections.title: Ask for two proposals covering the same work
paragraphs:
If Flex is attractive because your volume varies, ask AnswerUSA to quote that route and a named plan for one identical scope. Keep the request consistent: the same business, call types, coverage window, destinations and tasks. Otherwise a smaller bill may simply represent less work.

For example, a fictional window-installation business might need reception while its owner conducts site visits. A new caller requests an estimate, an existing customer asks about an arranged visit and a supplier wants to speak with the office. Write down the authorized result for each before discussing packages. Do not ask a receptionist to promise installation dates, approve technical details or accept work outside the business's rules.

Use the comparison record below. Empty cells are questions for the actual quote, not evidence that a feature is absent.

| Purchasing item | Flex proposal | Named plan proposal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact offer and effective date | Confirm in writing | Record Starter, Business or Executive and version |
| Required payment | Obtain amount, due date and conditions | Obtain base amount and billing interval |
| Chargeable unit | Confirm what is counted and when | Confirm unit, allowance and reset rule |
| Additional work | Identify separately priced activities | Identify exclusions and additional usage |
| Permitted reception tasks | Record the agreed scope | Record the same scope for comparison |
| Change and exit | Obtain applicable method and timing | Obtain applicable method and timing |

The supplier may determine that a route is unsuitable for the requested work. Record that conclusion and its reason rather than forcing an artificial like-for-like price comparison.

sections.title: Model uncertain volume without pretending it is known
paragraphs:
Use a quieter period and a busier period from records your business is authorized to inspect. Separate observed activity from a new-work forecast. A short history is not a forecast.

Then ask how each quoted route would charge those same records under its own rules. A count of calls does not automatically equal a minute allowance, and time spent talking is not necessarily the entire contractual measure. Obtain the actual definition and treatment of short calls, transfers, repeated inquiries and other requested work rather than copying another supplier's definitions.

Where an amount or rule is missing, do not calculate a false total. Keep the unresolved line visible, assign a person to obtain it and determine whether the uncertainty prevents a purchase. The useful result is an auditable proposal comparison, not an impressive-looking number assembled from assumptions.

The [general pay-as-you-go guide](/ai-answering-service/pay-as-you-go-answering-service) explains model-level questions. This decision requires AnswerUSA's actual Flex and named-plan offers for the same reception work.

sections.title: Establish what happens after the operator answers
paragraphs:
AnswerUSA's homepage lists scheduling, service dispatch, employee call-ins and other services. Those categories are not verified entitlements for every plan. An installation company requesting only customer reception should identify that scope; an employer also requesting staff call-ins should have the additional work identified separately.

A service label is not an acceptance record. For the fictional installation business, ask AnswerUSA to demonstrate the outputs below using authorized, invented inquiries. This guide has not performed those demonstrations.

| Fictional inquiry | Evidence the office should inspect | Decision retained by the business |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New installation estimate request | Captured details, service-area result and actual destination | Whether and when the estimate is accepted |
| Existing visit change | Identified job or appointment and permitted change procedure | Who authorizes the revised commitment |
| Unavailable office recipient | Attempt record, delivered message and unresolved outcome | Who owns the next response |

If scheduling is requested, distinguish a preferred time from a calendar entry the business recognizes as booked. If a call is relayed, distinguish contact with the office from acceptance by a technician. Get the selected account's system, permissions and limitations into the proposal instead of assuming that a broad service description settles them.

sections.title: Keep the accepted route connected to daily ownership
paragraphs: Retain the chosen Flex, Starter, Business or Executive proposal beside the approved instructions. Name an account owner and the person checking daily requests. Before changing routes, ask how the price, permitted work, effective date and instructions change; do not infer the process from the word “flexibility.”

sections.title: Where Revo belongs in the comparison
paragraphs:
AnswerUSA's staffed route deserves consideration when the business needs supplier-provided human reception for the agreed work. Revo can be evaluated when its published AI answering, intake, supported booking and summaries meet the requirement. Team transfers and additional features depend on the selected Revo plan and configuration.

This guide does not claim Revo supplies human receptionists, has an AnswerUSA connection, provisions a phone system or shares AnswerUSA's billing or agreement conditions. A buyer requiring a capability that Revo has not established should keep that requirement visible rather than treating a pricing CTA as proof of equivalence.

sections.title: Frequently asked questions
paragraphs:
### Does Flex mean there can be no agreement or other charge?

No. Confirm the actual terms and chargeable work. The public Flex statement concerns minimums and commitment to monthly minute plans, not every possible condition.

### Can I choose between the three named plans from their names?

No. The reviewed page does not publish the numerical or functional differences needed to make that choice. Obtain proposals for your actual scope.

### Is this a review based on using AnswerUSA?

No. It is a documentary purchasing guide from a competing provider. No service test, customer-rating consensus or savings result is claimed.

[Review Revo's current plans](/pricing) alongside AnswerUSA's completed two-route comparison and the work your office is prepared to retain.

Ask which service is being quoted and which described actions belong in that specific agreement. A business may need incoming coverage without buying broader administration. Another may need an authorized person to maintain records, making ordinary message delivery an incomplete substitute.

sections.title: Treat the cost projection as a procurement artifact
paragraphs:
The supplier's [No Surprises Pledge](https://suite1000.com/no-surprises-pledge) promises a total cost projection per billing cycle before engagement. This is a published supplier promise, not an independently verified billing result. The reviewed pages do not supply a numeric tariff, cycle length or complete policy for changes in scope and volume.

A useful projection should identify the assignment it prices. Request the assumptions behind it and ask what happens when those assumptions change. Do not turn the word “projection” into an invented fixed-price cap, refund right or guaranteed invoice amount.

sections.title: Start with the billing rules, not an invented tariff
paragraphs:
[Southwest’s published terms](https://southwestansweringservice.com/terms-of-service/) describe 28-day invoices, recurring base charges in advance and overage or quantity-based services afterward. Calls have a 60-second minimum and 60-second billing increments, measured from connection to disconnection. Inbound and outbound actions, programming and account-management time can be chargeable. No complete dollar tariff is established by the reviewed pages.

The terms also reserve holiday charges subject to the agreement. Ask for the actual proposal’s definitions and rates. Do not assume that every action discussed during a sales conversation is included in the recurring base.

A contractor office should identify which work creates usage before comparing a provider that meters only a different set of activities. A lower quoted rate is not automatically a lower bill when the measured work differs.

sections.title: Normalize the calendar using real dates
paragraphs:
A 28-day cycle is four weeks. Thirteen such periods span 364 days, but that calculation does not establish how many invoices land in your particular calendar year. Activation dates, advance billing and the period being budgeted matter.

For a useful comparison, choose a start date and an end date. Ask the provider to show which recurring charges and usage charges fall inside that window. Use the same window for an answering service that bills by calendar month.

Keep usage and cash timing in separate columns. A usage charge invoiced after the covered period may arrive later than the base charge for that same service period. Your office needs both the service budget and the payment schedule.

sections.title: Turn the proposed workload into a quote worksheet
paragraphs:
Use real call records where available, with unnecessary personal information removed. Do not assume that one supplier’s billed minutes are equivalent to another supplier’s measured minutes.

| Budget field | Record for Southwest’s actual quote | Check before comparison |
|---|---|---|
| Service window | Activation and end dates | Use identical dates for every proposal |
| Recurring base | Amount and covered dates | Separate service period from invoice date |
| Call measurement | Minimum, increment and start/stop definition | Recalculate the same sample calls |
| Staff contact | Any outbound calls or follow-up activity | Identify what adds to billed work |
| Configuration | Programming and account-management activities | Ask which changes incur charges |
| Other coverage | Applicable holidays and requested services | Record specific amounts or unresolved terms |
| Usage charges | Rate and when billed | Keep later invoices visible in cash planning |
| Change control | Who authorizes a chargeable account change | Avoid conflicting office instructions |

For example, a service manager might ask the provider to add a second recipient, change an on-call destination and revise the handling of appointment questions. Record those as three requested changes and ask what is billable. This example does not establish that Southwest charges a particular fee for any one change.

sections.title: Establish an exit and invoice-review owner
paragraphs:
The published terms describe an initial 84-day term, then cycle-to-cycle renewal with 28 days’ written cancellation notice. They also specify a 28-day window for written invoice disputes. Confirm the dates and process in the proposed agreement rather than treating this summary as a determination of legal rights or enforceability.

Give one office role responsibility for tracking the activation date, reviewing invoices and keeping any notices. A field technician who receives a message is not necessarily the person authorized to dispute a charge or end an account.

| Administrative event | Office action | Evidence to retain |
|---|---|---|
| Proposed start | Confirm the actual service activation date | Accepted proposal and activation confirmation |

sections.title: Evaluate the actual reception outcome as well
paragraphs:
A complete budget is useful only for a service that fits the office’s calls. Define what happens to a new inquiry, an existing-job question and a request requiring a team member. Distinguish a delivered message from a recipient accepting responsibility or a technician attending the property.

Southwest’s contractor and service descriptions should be checked against the purchased configuration. This guide does not verify emergency response, field dispatch outcomes or guaranteed handling during a surge.

Revo offers AI reception for inbound calls. Its current plans describe appointment booking and configured scripts, hours and rules; team transfers depend on plan. Revo is not presented as a supplier of Southwest’s live staff or as having the same billable-work definitions. Compare the same supported tasks and workload before choosing.

paragraphs:

The calendar differs. Compare charges over the same actual service dates, including applicable usage and other charges, rather than comparing base labels alone.

### Is a current Southwest dollar price established here?

No. Request a quote for the required work. The reviewed terms establish billing rules, not a complete tariff for your business.

### Does changing an instruction necessarily cost extra?

The terms include programming and account-management work in chargeable scope. Ask which proposed changes are included or billed under your actual agreement; this guide does not assign a fee to a particular edit.

No. Confirm the proposed agreement and obtain qualified advice if needed. The worksheet helps the office collect dates and evidence, not determine legal enforceability.

| Field | Main office | Second office or service branch |
|---|---|---|
| Account identifier | Provider-confirmed identifier | Provider-confirmed identifier |
| Approved greeting | Exact business wording | Exact branch wording |
| Service boundary | Accepted requests and area | Accepted requests and area |
| Required intake | Fields needed for useful follow-up | Branch-specific differences |
| Routine recipient | Person or office role | Person or office role |
| Unavailable recipient | Approved fallback | Approved fallback |
| Instruction owner | Who can request a change | Who can request a change |
| Billing treatment | Written account and usage terms | Written account and usage terms |

For example, a homeowner may contact the wrong branch about an existing appointment. Define whether the service should capture the request, identify the proper office or use a supported transfer. Do not assume a separate account automatically gives an agent access to every branch’s calendar or job records.

## Include work with your staff in the usage discussion

An incoming call can create additional communication after the original conversation ends. Because Keystone describes pricing in terms of agent work with callers and staff, ask how each proposed follow-up activity is measured.

Use the same set of scenarios when comparing proposals:

- A new inquiry that requires only a delivered message.

- A request sent to an unavailable staff member.
- A correction to an on-call destination or staff record.

## Verify portal updates through a controlled example

|---|---|---|
| Change one branch’s recipient | Resulting account instructions | Other branches changed too |
| Update a staff record | Provider-confirmed effective information | Every related field updated automatically |
| Review a sample message | Account identity, request and delivery record | Delivery proves business responsibility accepted |
| Remove an old staff contact | Confirmed removal and remaining destination | Every historic record or permission disappeared |
| End service | Applicable notice and effective date | Stopping forwarding ends the agreement |

sections.title: Separate access, included calls and extra work
paragraphs:
TCB's [FAQ](https://www.tcbanswering.com/faq) describes a base access charge, optional monthly call packages and usage billed in arrears. Its [pricing page](https://www.tcbanswering.com/pricing) identifies calls above a selected package as overcalls. sections.title: Build a purchase worksheet around your office's calls
paragraphs:
Start with an anonymized representative period. Keep new inquiries, existing-job questions and requested changes recognizable as different tasks. This worksheet asks for contractual answers; it does not state that every action is included in a TCB plan.

| Purchase component | Office input | Supplier answer to record | Evidence to retain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base access | Coverage period and desired availability | Charge, billing period and what access includes | The dated base-service line |
| Included-call package | Representative call count and likely variation | Selected allowance and definition of a counted call | Package description and usage rules |
| Overcalls | A period above the proposed allowance | Applicable rate and which events create extra calls | The relevant rate and example classification |
| Scheduling | The exact permitted booking or change | Whether the task is purchased and how access works | Scope and responsibility for exceptions |
| Software or custom forms | Fields the office needs recorded | Included work, configuration and additional charge | Approved field list and quote item |
| Package change | A proposed increase or decrease | Notice required, effective date and affected usage | Written confirmation of the change |
| Exit | The desired final coverage date | Notice process, final billing and end of service | Supplier acknowledgement and final instructions |

Do not put sensitive customer records into a supplier evaluation simply to complete the table. Use fictional examples for demonstrations and provide only the operational information needed through your normal procurement process.

sections.title: Ask which period a package change actually affects
paragraphs:
TCB describes package flexibility for changing needs. That statement does not establish same-month effectiveness, retrospective repricing or automatic selection of the cheapest package. Billing in arrears alone does not settle any of those questions.

For example, an office might expect a busier period and ask to increase its allowance. Record the request date, the requested effective date and the supplier's confirmed effective date as separate fields. Ask which calls would fall under the old package and which under the new one. Keep the same distinction if reducing coverage afterward.

If the supplier does not resolve the timing, leave it unknown in the cost comparison. Do not assume a late change removes overcalls already incurred. The purpose is to understand the actual policy before depending on it, rather than turn flexibility into an unsupported savings claim.

sections.title: Keep task scope separate from the call counter
paragraphs:
A caller asking for an estimate and a caller requesting a change to tomorrow's visit might each count as a call, yet require different work. Decide whether your office needs a message, an authorized calendar action or information entered into another system.

Use a fictional existing-job correction to discuss the proposed configuration. Ask where the corrected information would appear, who would receive it and what happens when the office must approve the next step. A completed form does not by itself prove an appointment changed or a technician accepted responsibility.

Confirm how the required work appears in the proposal. If scheduling or external-software access is separately scoped, show it separately when comparing offers. Our [per-call versus per-minute guide](/ai-answering-service/compare/per-call-vs-per-minute-answering-service) explains billing-unit arithmetic; this worksheet establishes what the specific TCB arrangement would buy before applying any arithmetic.

sections.title: Plan the exit before forwarding the line
paragraphs:
The reviewed FAQ states an initial 30-day contract period and requires 30 days' written notice to cancel. Those terms should remain visible alongside package flexibility. Being able to change a package does not mean service can necessarily end immediately.

Request the accepted notice method, the date service would end and how final usage is billed. Assign an office owner to confirm that caller routing will reach the intended destination when coverage changes. Preserve a copy of the notice and the supplier's response. Do not assume that stopping call forwarding, reducing traffic or requesting a smaller package constitutes cancellation.

sections.title: Compare Revo for the same supported outcome
paragraphs:
Revo publishes AI answering, intake, appointment booking and call summaries, with features and transfers dependent on the selected plan and supported configuration. Its [current plans](/pricing) provide the relevant offer details. This guide does not establish Revo per-call billing, TCB-style package changes, supplier-provided humans or arbitrary software access.

Compare the portion of reception work each actual offer supports. Keep any additional administrative assignment, office follow-up and contractual commitment visible. A lower allowance price cannot resolve a mismatch in the task you need completed.

sections.title: Frequently asked questions
paragraphs:
### Can a TCB package change reprice calls from earlier in the month?

The reviewed pages do not establish retrospective repricing. Ask which usage period the confirmed change affects.

### Does 24/7 access prove every additional task or holiday charge is included?

No. Availability, task scope and charges are separate terms. Confirm the selected offer rather than inferring inclusions from coverage hours.

### Does cancelling forwarding end the agreement?

Do not assume so. The reviewed FAQ requires written cancellation notice; confirm the applicable process and final service date with the supplier.

sections.title: Identify the exchange you are buying
paragraphs:
[Aspire's service page](https://aspireansweringservice.com/answering_service.html) advertises interactive text messaging between its operators and the client's staff, alongside message delivery and call relay or patching. Revo plans include a monthly minute allowance, and calls under 20 seconds do not count. Every plan answers 24/7, books appointments with your rules, sends SMS follow-up and logs call summaries, from $87.50/mo at launch. You keep your number and forward calls. [See Revo's plans](/pricing)

title: eVoice Alternatives: Phone System or Reception Service?
description: Compare eVoice alternatives for home services by separating business phone features, live receptionist coverage, and the reception tasks your office needs.
lead: If you are comparing eVoice alternatives for a home service business, start with what you want to replace. A business phone number, an automated phone menu, and a person answering customer calls are different purchases. Replacing the reception task does not necessarily replace the phone system behind it.
intro: If you are comparing eVoice alternatives for a home service business, start with what you want to replace. A business phone number, an automated phone menu, and a person answering customer calls are different purchases. Replacing the reception task does not necessarily replace the phone system behind it.

sections.title: Separate eVoice's phone plans from its live receptionist service
paragraphs:
[eVoice's pricing page](https://www.evoice.com/pricing/) describes business phone plans. Its advertised features include business calling and number-management functions. Those plans should not be read as the price of a human receptionist answering every incoming inquiry.

The separate [live receptionist service](https://www.evoice.com/live-receptionist/) describes a US-based team, appointment handling, and service customized to the business. It describes per-minute billing and publishes availability as 8 a.m.–8 p.m. EST, with virtual handling after hours. Confirm the applicable days, holiday schedule, time-zone treatment, and handling outside that window in your proposal. The published hour label does not establish round-the-clock human coverage.

That distinction changes the comparison. If you need extensions and business calling, evaluate a phone service against those requirements. If you need someone to receive an estimate request while your crew is working, compare the reception workflow as its own scope.

sections.title: Keep the phone functions you still need
paragraphs:
Use this worksheet before moving a number or canceling a service. These are proposed purchasing checks, not tests we performed.

| Requirement | What to establish before switching |
| --- | --- |
| Business number and outbound calling | Which provider supplies them and what remains available after the change |
| Extensions or an automated menu | Whether the replacement supports the same routing your staff actually uses |
| A new customer's estimate request | What may be booked, what is only collected, and who receives the result |
| Calls outside staffed hours | Whether a human, automated system, or AI service handles the call |
| An existing customer's unresolved issue | Who owns the follow-up and what information reaches that person |

Do not assume that an AI receptionist includes number porting, a complete business phone system, or every messaging feature in your current plan. Keep those requirements in the written comparison.

sections.title: Compare the reception offer on its own terms
paragraphs:
Revo offers 24/7 AI reception with business instructions, appointment booking, SMS follow-up, and call summaries. Team transfers and software connections depend on the selected plan. Confirm the exact supported workflow before choosing a plan or changing your existing phone arrangement.

For eVoice's live service, request the receptionist allowance, chargeable minutes, overage terms, and coverage schedule. For Revo, review the current plan and its applicable limits. Give both suppliers the same description of the calls your office needs handled. Neither a phone-plan headline nor an answered-call count proves a completed service appointment.

Also check the terms attached to the particular purchase. eVoice's live receptionist page excludes that service from its money-back guarantee. Do not carry a guarantee advertised for a phone plan over to the receptionist add-on.

sections.title: Choose the arrangement your office can operate
paragraphs: Keep a phone service when its calling and routing functions remain necessary. Choose human reception when that model and its agreed coverage fit the conversations your customers bring. Consider Revo when your reception rules and supported actions fit an AI service. The useful alternative is the arrangement that preserves the required phone functions and gives each unresolved call an owner.

sections.title: Frequently asked questions
paragraphs:
### Is eVoice's standard phone plan the same as its live receptionist service?
No. Its public pages present a business phone offer and a separate live receptionist service. Request the terms for the specific services you intend to buy.

### Does eVoice advertise 24/7 human answering on the live receptionist page?
The reviewed page publishes 8 a.m.–8 p.m. EST and describes virtual handling after hours. Confirm the complete schedule directly rather than assuming 24/7 human coverage.

### Can Revo replace every eVoice phone feature?
Do not assume full phone-system equivalence. Match your number, calling, routing, messaging, and reception requirements to the applicable offer. [Review Revo's current plans](/pricing).

Sources reviewed November 4, 2026: [eVoice](https://www.evoice.com/), [phone pricing](https://www.evoice.com/pricing/), [live receptionist service](https://www.evoice.com/live-receptionist/), and [Revo plans](https://www.revoapp.ai/pricing). Supplier descriptions are not independent performance evidence.
