sections.title: Decide which Bland offer is in the comparison
paragraphs:
[Bland's platform pricing](https://www.bland.ai/pricing) presents usage-based plans with different platform fees, minute rates, transfer rates, and capacity allowances. The total depends on the selected plan and the calls it processes. A per-minute headline is not, by itself, the full cost of running your reception workflow.

The separate [Agent Phone Plan documentation](https://docs.bland.ai/platform/agent-phone-plan) describes its own subscription and account-wide call limits. The reviewed documentation lists one concurrent call and additional call-frequency limits. If your purchase uses this product, establish what a second caller experiences while a call is already active. Do not substitute the larger voice platform's concurrency allowance for the phone plan's limits.

The reviewed official pages also contain inconsistent starting-price presentations for the agent phone offer. We therefore do not present one of those figures as a definitive universal price. Ask Bland to identify the current offer, applicable recurring price, introductory period, and governing terms in writing.

sections.title: Compare the product, the capacity, and the owner
paragraphs:
This is a proposed evaluation worksheet, not a completed benchmark.

| Buying decision | Evidence to request |
| --- | --- |
| Voice platform or Agent Phone Plan | The exact product and plan named in the order |
| Two customers call together | The applicable concurrency limit and the second caller's experience |
| A call needs a staff handoff | Transfer behavior, unanswered-call handling, and the relevant charges |
| Your office changes its service area | Who updates the instructions and verifies the resulting behavior |
| The requested appointment cannot be confirmed | What the caller is told and who receives the unresolved request |

[Bland's home services page](https://www.bland.ai/industries/home-services) describes uses across trades such as HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and cleaning. Those descriptions support evaluating the product for a contractor's workflow. They do not prove that your particular scheduling system, exception rules, or capacity requirements are already configured.

sections.title: Compare reception responsibility as well as usage cost
paragraphs:
Revo offers 24/7 AI reception with business instructions, appointment booking, SMS follow-up, and call summaries. Transfers and software connections depend on the selected plan. This does not establish feature parity with Bland's configurable platform or an equivalent concurrency allowance.

If your team has implementation support and wants to control a configurable voice workflow, include that work in the Bland proposal. If your immediate goal is a defined inbound reception service, compare the supported Revo workflow against the same caller requests. In either case, establish who maintains the instructions and handles exceptions after launch.

Use a written scope for estimate requests, booking authority, and handoff. A receptionist should not promise a price, crew arrival, or appointment change that your business has not authorized. Ask each supplier to demonstrate the supported outcome without treating a demonstration as evidence of guaranteed production results.

No. The reviewed pages describe different offers and limits. Compare the exact product you intend to purchase.

### Why is there no single Bland price in this comparison?
Platform costs depend on the plan and usage, and the reviewed agent phone price presentations conflict. Obtain the applicable current terms rather than building a savings calculation from an uncertain starting price.

### How should I compare Revo with Bland?
Agree on the reception tasks, required connections, handoff behavior, and operating responsibility first. Then compare the complete offers. [Review Revo's current plans](/pricing).

title: Lindy Pricing: Budget for Reception and Shared Credits
description: Understand Lindy pricing for home service reception: paid seats, shared credits, phone usage, and what to confirm before comparing a reception plan.
lead: Lindy pricing needs a closer look when your home service office wants phone reception inside a broader AI workspace. The relevant question is how the people using that workspace and the work consuming its credits affect the calls your office needs answered.
intro: Lindy pricing needs a closer look when your home service office wants phone reception inside a broader AI workspace. The relevant question is how the people using that workspace and the work consuming its credits affect the calls your office needs answered.

sections.title: Follow the shared credit pool
paragraphs:
[Lindy's phone product page](https://www.lindy.ai/product/phone) describes US phone numbers and calls, including inbound reception and calendar-related workflows. Its phone FAQ says calls consume credits by minute from the same pool used for other work.

The reviewed [pricing page](https://www.lindy.ai/pricing) describes paid active seats and a shared credit allowance. It also explains that credit-consuming actions pause when the available credits run out. That makes the reception budget depend partly on what else your workspace does.

Do not convert a credit allowance into a promised number of phone minutes without the applicable conversion and configuration. We have not verified one universal phone-credit conversion that would justify that calculation. A monthly subscription headline alone does not establish the cost of answering your expected calls.

sections.title: Confirm the applicable offer before using a starting price
paragraphs:
The official pages reviewed for this comparison show inconsistent starting-price presentations across the broader product. Rather than treating one figure as a fixed receptionist price, obtain the offer for your intended workspace, active seats, and phone use.

Ask whether the quote includes the relevant phone setup, how usage draws down credits, and what happens as the balance approaches zero. The reviewed pricing terms distinguish monthly credits, which reset, from purchased top-ups. Verify the current top-up and renewal conditions for the offer you select.

sections.title: Make reception visible inside the workspace budget
paragraphs:
The following is a purchasing worksheet, not a measured Lindy workload.

| Budget item | Question for your proposal |
| --- | --- |
| Active users | Which people create a paid seat, and who administers access? |
| Shared credits | Which other tasks consume the same allowance as phone work? |
| Phone consumption | What is the applicable credit treatment for your configured calls? |
| Low balance | What warning and replenishment process protects the supported workflow? |
| A paused action | What operational fallback should your office use? |

A remodeling office might want one workspace for reception and other administrative tasks. That can be relevant to its purchase, but the office still needs a clear owner for the reception allowance and any interruption. Do not assume that unused capacity elsewhere guarantees continuous phone handling.

sections.title: Separate a product illustration from your approved workflow
paragraphs:

description: Cover Saturdays, Sundays and holidays without staff by the phone: what a weekend answering service should book, escalate and tell callers.

intro: Homeowners notice problems on weekends, when they are home. A weekend answering service lets you answer those calls without paying someone to sit by the phone all Saturday.

sections.title: Decide what gets booked and what gets escalated
paragraphs:
Most weekend calls are not emergencies. They are quote requests, maintenance questions and jobs that can wait for a weekday slot. Book those straight into your calendar so the caller hangs up with a time.

Keep a short escalation list for the calls that cannot wait, such as active leaks or no heat. Those go to the person on call, and everything else waits for Monday.

sections.title: Tell callers what happens on Monday
paragraphs: A weekend caller who hears nothing specific often keeps dialing other companies. The script should say what happens next in plain words: who will call, which day and what they will confirm. If the job is booked, repeat the day and the address before the call ends.

sections.title: Plan holiday schedules ahead
paragraphs:
A holiday answering service needs the same rules as weekends, plus a calendar. Before each holiday, update three things:

- **Your hours**, so callers hear that the office is closed that day.
- **Your on-call contact**, if it changes for the holiday.
- **Your first open slot**, so bookings land on a day the crew is working.

Changing these a week early avoids booking jobs on a day nobody is working.

sections.title: Where Revo fits
paragraphs: Revo answers forwarded calls 24/7, including weekends and holidays, and books appointments with your script, hours and rules. It sends SMS follow-up and logs a summary of every call on your dashboard, so Monday starts with a list instead of voicemails. Crew and Fleet add transfers to your team. sections.title: Frequently asked questions

markdownArticle.content:
# How an AI Receptionist for Small Business UK Handles Calls

For a small business in the UK, missing calls can mean lost opportunities. An AI receptionist for small business UK answers every call, follows your script, and handles appointments, so you never miss a customer—even outside regular hours.

Published by Revo, which sells an AI receptionist for home service businesses. Reviewed November 10, 2026.

## How Calls Are Answered and Routed
When a customer calls your business, the AI receptionist answers promptly, using your chosen greeting and script. It can respond in English or Spanish, ensuring callers feel understood. If your plan includes it, important calls can be transferred directly to your team, so urgent matters reach the right person.

## Appointment Booking and Call Summaries
The AI receptionist books appointments directly into your calendar or field service software, following your rules. After each call, it sends a summary to your team, so you always know who called and why. This keeps your schedule organised and your team informed, without extra admin work.

## Follow-Up and Communication
After every call, the AI receptionist sends an SMS follow-up to the caller, confirming their appointment or next steps. For businesses using WhatsApp, messages can also be sent there. This helps keep customers engaged, reduces no-shows, and ensures everyone is on the same page.

## Where Revo fits
Revo answers the calls you forward to it, 24/7, and follows your script and rules. It books appointments, sends SMS follow-up and logs a summary of every call. On Crew and Fleet it can transfer calls to your team and connect to your field service software. Plans start from $87.50/mo at launch. [See Revo's plans](/pricing)

## Frequently asked questions
### Can the AI receptionist give quotes or prices over the phone?
No, it does not provide quotes or pricing information to callers. It can book appointments and answer questions within your script.
### Does the AI receptionist assign technicians or jobs?
No, it does not assign technicians or dispatch jobs. It handles call answering, appointment booking, and follow-up.
